Total number of days in September with at least 100 degrees: 8 days. Prior to 2022, only 8 days reached or exceeded 100 degrees in September through the ENTIRE climate history of Reno, which goes back to 1888. This far exceeded the previous record of 3   days in September 2017 with highs at least 100��F.

Warmest September Temperature: 106��F. This surpassed the highest temperature ever reported in September (and even August), and was equal to the 4th hottest day in  Reno`s climate history (only surpassed by three days with 108��F on July 10-11, 2002 and July 5, 2007). Warmest minimum temperature for any September day: 69��F on  the 7th, surpassing the previous record of 67��F.

On Sept. 7, 2024, the Davis Fire broke out around 2:30 p.m. in the area of Davis Creek Regional Park located 20 miles south of Reno, Nevada. This wind-driven fire rapidly burned a total of 5,824 acres of private, state, and federal lands, destroying two commercial buildings, 14 residences, and 22 outbuildings. Truckee Meadows Fire Protection District, Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest, and Bureau of Land Management managed the fire under a unified command. Due to the fire���s complexity, the Southwest Area Incident Management Team 1 was order and took over the management of the fire the evening of Monday, Sept. 9, and transferred it back to a local Type 4 organization on Thursday, Sept. 18. The fire was officially called 100 percent contained at 6 p.m. on Wednesday, Sept. 25.

Strong synoptic-scale winds moving across the Sierra Nevada spread into western Nevada the evening of December 18th.  The strongest wind gusts occurred after midnight and through the morning hours of the 19th.  From approximately 230 am PST and 245 am PST wind gusts to 123 knots (142 mph) were recorded at the summit of Virginia Peak (elev. 8299 ft).  The NWS Reno WSR-88D weather radar sits atop Virginia Peak.  The radome (which protects the radar transmitter from the elements) was buckled inward by the strong wind gusts.  This caused the radar transmitter to stop rotating, thus shutting down the radar.

Wind gusts to 82 knots (94 mph) were recorded on the summit of Virginia Peak (elev. 8299 ft), the location of the NWS Reno WSR-88D weather radar which was damaged by strong winds on December 19th.  The wind gusted to 94 mph during a one-and-a-half-hour period from approximately 215 am PST to 330 am PST Christmas morning.  These strong winds further damaged the radome and the now-exposed radar transmitter.  Most of the fiberglass radome was torn from the radar pedestal and fell to the ground.  Exposed to the force of the wind, the radar transmitter was damaged beyond repair.

Rainfall amounts from the evening of May 1st through the morning of May 3rd totaled over 2.00 inches at some locations:||Ward Creek SNOTEL near Alpine Meadows, 2.80 inches; |3 miles ENE of Alpine Meadows, 2.00 inches; |3 miles east of Donner Peak, 1.99 inches; |Squaw Valley SNOTEL, 1.70 inches; and |Tahoe City, 1.22 inches.

Heavy rainfall over Nevada County caused river and creek levels to rise. Some 24-hour rainfall totals included:||5 miles WNW of Truckee, 2.57 inches of rain caused minor street flooding; |Donner Lake HADS site 5 miles west of Truckee (elev. 5924 ft), 1.87 inches; and |Independence Creek SNOTEL (elev. 6500 ft), 1.30 inches.

The Galena RAWS recorded a wind gust of 62 knots (71 mph). Wind gusts of 50 knots or greater were recorded from 700 pm PDT on May 4th through 400 am PDT May 5th.  The Nevada Dept. of Transportation (NDOT) weather sensor in Washoe Valley recorded a wind gust of 56 knots (65 mph). Wind gusts of 50 knots or greater were recorded from 1239 am through 149 am PDT on May 5th.
A trained weather spotter reported that a 20-ft tall 2-ft diameter tree was blown down onto a fence. Numerous small branches from other trees were also broken by the strong wind gusts.

A trained weather spotter reported wind gusts to 43 knots (50 mph) near Fallon Station. The strong wind produced blowing dust which reduced visibility to around 3 miles. A tree was blown over onto a power line which resulted in a loss of power for a few minutes.
A 56 knot (64 mph) wind gust was recorded at the Lovelock airport.
A trained weather spotter reported 1-inch diameter hail 3 miles SSW of Gardnerville.
A trained weather spotter reported 1-inch diameter hail in Cromberg.
Nickel-size hail was reported 2 miles south of Sierraville.
A dust devil was observed in a field west of Pyramid Highway at Calle de la Plata north of Reno.

The Plumas County Sheriff's Department reported that a woman was struck by lightning at her home in Portola.  She was transported by helicopter to the U.C. Davis Medical Center.  She never regained consciousness and died from her injuries on June 11th.
A trained weather spotter located 3 miles southeast of Fallon reported hail of 1-inch diameter.

A wildfire covering approximately 14 acres threatened homes in the Eastlake Boulevard and Douglas Boulevard area in Washoe Valley.  The Reno Gazette-Journal reported that the fire had burned to within 200 feet of at least one of the homes.  The fire was thought to have been started by a lightning strike.
A trained weather spotter reported three-quarter-inch hail between Sun Valley and Sparks.
The Churchill County Sheriff's Office reported flash flooding near Middlegate Station.  The flash flooding was affecting Nevada Highway 722 and U.S. Highway 50 between Eastgate and Middlegate.

The Nevada Dept. of Transportation (NDOT) weather sensor in Washoe Valley recorded a wind gust of 69 mph. Additional wind gusts of 60 mph or greater were recorded at the site from 340 pm PDT through 440 pm PDT.  The Galena RAWS recorded a wind gust of 51 knots (59 mph).
The Galena RAWS recorded a wind gust of 62 kt (71 mph) at an elevation of 5610 feet. The outflow was from thunderstorms over Lake Tahoe.
The Nevada DOT wind sensor near Toulon recorded a wind gust of 60 kt (69 mph).

A strong thunderstorm downdraft damaged two aircraft at the Soar Truckee facility at the Truckee-Tahoe Airport.  The wind gust destroyed an SGS 2-33 aircraft and damaged another glider.  No gliders were airborne at the time and no one was injured.
Hail 1-inch in diameter was reported in Cold Springs northwest of Reno.

Strong winds were recorded across the area.  The Reno Gazette-Journal reported that the strong winds caused a semi-trailer to blow over on U. S. Highway 395 near Stead.  An off-duty NWS employee reported a portion of a fence blown down in the Spanish Springs area northeast of Reno.  The Nevada DOT sensor at Five Mile Flat near Virginia City recorded a wind gust of 69 mph at 6:45 am PDT.  Also, the Galena RAWS recorded a wind gust of 66 mph at 11:03 am PDT.
The Bridgeport RAWS recorded a wind gust of 65 mph while the Walker RAWS recorded a wind gust to 59 mph.

The Nevada Highway Patrol reported that the westbound lane of Interstate 80 was closed about 20 miles east of Fernley due to poor visibility caused by blowing dust.  Two tractor-trailer rigs ran off the road when the visibility was near zero.

A narrow lake effect snow band caused snowfall amounts of 4 to 8 inches on non-paved surfaces in the Smith Valley southwest of Yerington. However, there were few road impacts noted as low temperatures were in the 30s and road surfaces were relatively warm.||Some tree limbs, still laden with leaves, broke and fell on power lines due to the weight of the heavy, wet snow. Around 100 customers were without power in the Smith Valley on the 4th.

A narrow lake effect band brought 5 to 10 inches of snowfall to non-paved areas just south of Gardnerville.  There was little apparent travel impact as there were no road problems noted per web cams and the lack of chain or snow tire requirements through the event.
Four inches of snowfall were reported in Stateline.

A spotter just southwest of South Lake Tahoe reported 5 inches of snowfall. Four to five inches of snowfall was common to the south and east of Lake Tahoe (in the lake effect snow band), with up to 2 inches elsewhere around Lake Tahoe.

The Union newspaper in Grass Valley stated that the Coast Guard on Lake Tahoe responded to three capsized boats.  Buoys on Lake Tahoe recorded sustained winds of 35-40 mph with a few brief periods as high as 40-45 mph.
This wind gust was measured by a trained spotter 3 miles west of Loyalton.  The spotter also reported winds sustained at 50 mph.

Minor power outages were reported with these strong winds.  There were also isolated high wind gusts, mainly in typically wind-prone areas.  The isolated high wind reports include: Galena RAWS with 79 mph, Washoe Valley NDOT with 75 mph, Five Mile Flat NDOT with 71 mph, and the Reno ASOS with a very brief (less than 30 seconds) gust to 71 mph.
Urban street flooding was reported at 1830PST in the area of Double Diamond Pkwy, South Meadows Pkwy, and Double R Blvd.
A storm total of 4.93 inches of rainfall was recorded at the Alpine Meadows ALERT gauge (6910 feet elevation).

Very heavy, wet snow was followed by heavy rain and snow as snow levels rose to around 9500 feet late in the evening of October 13.  The heavy, wet snow knocked down some power lines and tree branches in the Mammoth Lakes area.  Snowfall totals before the switch to rain are as follows: 23 inches at the Mammoth Ski Area, 15 inches at the Leavitt Lake SNOTEL, and 12 inches at the Mammoth Lakes CO-OP.

Over 2 inches of rainfall caused damage to the Mono County Jail in Bridgeport.  The roof was being repaired and was not sufficiently protected from the unusually heavy rain.  Additional heavy rainfall amounts include: Crestview RAWS with 4.36, Benton RAWS with 2.86, and Mammoth Lakes Airport with 2.09.
A total of 3.33 inches of rain fell at the Markleeville RAWS on October 13 through early morning on October 14.

An intense but brief period of snow dropped modest snowfall amounts.  Here are some of the snowfall totals: 6-10 inches near the Sierra crest west of Lake Tahoe, Tahoe City with 5-8 inches, 5 inches for Truckee and South Lake Tahoe, and an estimated 3-6 inches from SNOTEL observations south and east of Lake Tahoe.

Overall, most of the area received 3 inches or less of snowfall on November 20.  However, isolated areas of Plumas and Sierra Counties received heavier amounts including 4 inches in Portola, 3.8 inches 3 miles SSW of Susanville, and approximately 6 inches 12 miles NW of Portola (on a ridge at 6900 feet).
The Lyon County Emergency Manager reported street flooding in Dayton at 1745PST.
The Lyon County Emergency Manager reported street flooding in Fernley at 1745PST.
Here are some snowfall amounts from November 20: Mt. Rose Ski Area with 8-10 inches, Big Meadow SNOTEL with an estimated 6-9 inches, and the Glenbrook CO-OP observer with 4 inches.

There were an exceptionally numerous and widespread number of high wind reports with this storm.  Here is a list of some of the highest reported gusts: 68 mph in the Carson Valley near Minden at 0920PST, 83 mph in southeast Reno at 0920PST and at the NWS in Reno at 1318PST, and 71 mph at the Reno-Tahoe International Airport at 1323PST. ||The high winds caused damage (trees, fences, and power lines) and power outages throughout the area, including 2,780 people in Carson City.  In addition, there were 4 flight cancellations and around a dozen flight delays at the Reno-Tahoe International Airport from 1300PST to 1500PST.

There were numerous high wind gust reports with this system.  Catnip Mt. had 60 mph at 1144PST, Buffalo Creek recorded 62 mph at 1159PST, Juniper Springs had 59 mph at 1240PST, and Gerlach reported 61 mph at 1314PST.

According to the Mineral County Independent News in Hawthorne, there was a power outage from 1500PST to 2100PST as well as some windows broken in Hawthorne.  A large part of a roof in Hawthorne was blown off. ||Here are some high wind gusts from the region: Schurz with 64 mph at 1133PST, Yerington AWOS with 59 at 1315PST, Brawley Peak RAWS (8080 ft elevation) with 76 mph at 1447PST, and Hawthorne AWOS with 72 mph at 1458PST.

Winds on Lake Tahoe were sustained at 40-50 mph.  There were no other sites which reached high wind criteria, however Kahle Drive and Glenbrook Canyon NDOT sensors recorded 45 and 47 mph gusts, respectively (gusts that high are notable given that these observations were in at least partially-sheltered locations).  Little Valley RAWS recorded a gust to 55 mph at 0838PST.

The Nevada Highway Patrol reported that, at 1218PST, near zero visibility caused a large accident on westbound Interstate 80 about 20 miles east of Fernley.  The accident involved 4 tractor trailer rigs, 3 pickups, and an SUV and caused one fatality along with 7 injuries.  Elsewhere, there were numerous trees and power lines down as well as major damage to one house in Fernley (due to fallen tree).||Here are some high wind gusts which contributed to the dust storm:  Pyramid Lake Fisheries with 60 mph at 1045PST, Silver Springs AWOS with 70 mph at 1315PST, and the Fallon ASOS with 59 mph at 1344PST.
Heavy rainfall caused a rock slide southeast of Yerington. A spotter reported a rock slide with boulders on the road in Wilson Canyon at 1830PST.
Heavy rain caused a rock slide on CA SR 89 just south of Meeks Bay.
Power outage, blowing dust, and 4-inch tree limbs down reported with high winds in Cedarville at 1120PST.

A spotter two miles west of Loyalton reported winds sustained at 55 mph with gusts to 65 mph at 1133PST.  Additional high wind gusts include: 67 mph at Bull Flat RAWS at 1059PST and 69 mph at Doyle RAWS at 1211PST.
Winds were sustained between 40-50 mph on Lake Tahoe.  Truckee AWOS recorded a gust to 64 mph at 1255PST.
Walker RAWS recorded a 78 mph wind gust at 1400PST. Other high wind gust observations include: Bridgeport AWOS with 60 mph at 1500PST and the Mammoth Airport AWOS with 68 mph at 2110PST.

Strong easterly upslope flow brought the most significant snowfall south of Lake Tahoe.  Areas near Lake Tahoe received 2 to 6 inches (locally up to 8 near the crest) while areas south of Lake Tahoe received 5 to 10 inches with local amounts up to 12 inches.

Strong easterly upslope flow into the Sierra allowed for a significant snowfall.  Here are some snowfall totals: Bridgeport CO-OP 6 inches, Mammoth Lakes Ranger Station |9 inches, Bodie State Park 14 inches, Leavitt Lake SNOTEL 16 inches, and the Mammoth Lakes Ski Area 11 inches.

Widespread breezy conditions with gusts 30 to 40 mph were reported with this system. An isolated high wind gust was reported at the Galena RAWS (wind-prone sensor), which had a gust to 67 mph between 0900PST and 1000PST.

A storm total of 2 to 3 feet of snowfall fell west of highway 89 and along the Sierra Crest, with 1 to 2 feet east of highway 89 and south of Lake Tahoe.  Here are some specific snowfall reports: Alpine Meadows Ski Area with 33-42 inches, 25 inches at the Truckee Airport, 18-20 inches for Tahoe City, and 13-15 inches for South Lake Tahoe.||In addition to heavy snowfall, wind gusts of 35-45 mph were recorded on the 6th between 1100PST and 1800PST with a 58 mph gust at the South Lake Tahoe airport at 1156PST.  Winds over the Sierra Crest gusted to between 90-100 mph.
Storm total snowfall reports ranged from 6 to 13 inches.  Here are some specific snowfall reports: 13 inches in Portola, 7-9 inches in Susanville, and 7 inches in Doyle.

This storm featured an intense, fairly short period of snowfall which affected areas mainly west of highway 395 and near the Sierra Crest with much less snowfall along and east of highway 395. Here are some snowfall totals: An estimated 24 inches at the Leavitt Lake SNOTEL, 13-16 at the Mammoth Lakes Ski Area and Mammoth Pass. Lesser amounts further east include the Mammoth Lakes Ranger Station with 10 inches and the Bridgeport CO-OP with 5 inches.

Some areas near the Sierra crest and along highway 395 experienced remarkably strong winds. The Mammoth Mountain ski area gusted to 142 mph between 1300PST and 1400PST.  Along highway 395, the Mammoth airport AWOS gusted to 93 mph at 1410PST while the Bridgeport RAWS gusted to 66 mph between 1300PST and 1400 PST.||In Lee Vining, a couple of car windows were broken by flying debris and an unsecured dumpster. Also, a road information sign was blown down onto a roadway. A wind gust to 56 mph was recorded at 1302PST.

The Big Meadow SNOTEL (4 miles S of Mogul at 8300 ft) had an estimated 18 inches of snowfall.  Other snowfall reports include: Mt Rose Ski Area with 23 inches, the Dagget Pass and Glenbrook fire stations with 17 inches apiece.  In addition to heavy snowfall, winds were gusting 30-45 mph around the onset of the winter storm.
Widespread totals of 6-10 inches were reported in the area. Here are some of the isolated higher totals: Carson City with 14-18 inches and Dayton with 13 inches.
A widespread 6-9 inches of snowfall fell generally south and west of Lovelock. Some specific totals include: 10-12 inches in Stagecoach, 9 inches in Fallon, and 6 inches in Fernley.

An observer in Yerington reported 4.5 to 5 inches of snowfall on the 7th, with schools being closed on the 8th.  A HADS observation 15 to 20 miles south of Hawthorne had an estimated 4-6 inches of snowfall.

Ten to 15 inches of snow fell in the higher terrain from Grizzly Ridge (NW of Portola) southward. Lesser amounts fell further north and east, including: Portola with 6 inches and Susanville with 5 inches.

In general, 1 to 2 feet of snow fell north and west of Lake Tahoe with 8 to 15 inches elsewhere, much of it from midday on the 12th through early morning on the 13th (12-16 hours). Here are some specific snowfall totals: 28 inches at the Northstar and Sugarbowl Ski areas, 20 inches at the Heavenly Ski Resort, 16 inches in Tahoe City and Truckee, and 9 inches at the South Lake Tahoe airport.

Fourteen to 28 inches of snowfall was reported with this system, mainly in the higher terrain west of highway 395, with 10 to 15 inches along highway 395 from Bridgeport to Mammoth Lakes. Specific snowfall tallies include: 28 inches one mile WNW of Mammoth Lakes, 24 inches at the Mammoth Ski Area, 15 inches at the Mammoth Lakes Ranger Station, and 10 inches at the Lee Vining CO-OP station.||In addition to heavy snowfall, sporadic gusty winds of 30-45 mph were recorded along highway 395 from Bridgeport south with an incredible 164 mph gust at the Mammoth Ski Area at 9950 feet (1900PST on the 12th).

This storm produced a average of 1 to 2 feet of snowfall. Here are some reports: Mount Rose Ski Area with 26 inches, Incline Village with 19.5 inches, Dagget Pass with 15 inches, and Glenbrook with 12 inches.

A solid 4 to 8 inches of snow fell with this system, especially in the foothills and north of highway 50. Here are some specific snowfall totals: 10 inches in NW Reno and Cold Springs Valley (Far NW Reno), 8 inches at the WFO Reno, 6 inches in Virginia City, and 4 inches at the Reno-Tahoe International airport.

This event was mostly rain (until end of storm) below 4500-5000 ft, with less than an inch in Susanville. Snowfall totals include: 18 inches at the Grizzly Ridge HADS (6900 ft), 14 at the Independence Ck SNOTEL (6500 ft), and 7 inches in Portola.

This event featured a very intense period of snowfall for the afternoon and evening of the 18th. For example, 12 and 14 inches of snowfall in 7 hours was recorded for the Lobdell Lake and Sonora Pass SNOTELs, respectively. Other snowfall totals for the entire event include: 25 at the Mammoth Ski Area, 13 inches at the Lee Vining CO-OP, 9 inches at Bodie State Park, and 5 inches in Bridgeport.||In addition to heavy snowfall, winds gusted over 120 mph atop Mammoth Mountain and between 35-45 mph at the Bridgeport RAWS and Mammoth AWOS (with one gust to 68 mph for Bridgeport). Finally, highway 395 was closed from 1730PST on the 18th until late on the 20th.

An estimated 14-20 inches of snow fell for the Mt. Rose Ski Area while Incline Village received 10 inches in only 7 hours. Lesser amounts fell further south, with only 3 inches for Glenbrook and Daggett Pass.||In addition to heavy snowfall, winds gusted between 35-50 mph for several sites in the Carson Range.

A widespread snowfall of 10 to 18 inches was reported per SNOTEL and CO-OP observations. The exceptions were near South Lake Tahoe where slightly warmer temperatures initially limited snowfall with around 8 inches at the Fallen Leaf SNOTEL.||In addition to snowfall, wind gusts to 90 mph were reported over the Sierra Crest while gusty winds of 30-45 mph were recorded from the Truckee AWOS, Alpine Meadows Ski Area, and South Lake Tahoe ASOS.

A majority of the following snow totals fell in approximately 12 hours: 3WNW Sierraville with 16 inches, 10-14 inches at the Independence Ck. SNOTEL and Grizzly Ridge HADS, 8 inches at the Portola CO-OP, and 4 inches 3SSW Susanville (CoCoRAHS).

An intense period of snow caused the closure of Interstate 80 from approximately 1340PST to 1610PST with numerous spinouts cited as the reason. Here are a few snowfall totals (most within 12 hours): 24 inches at the Homewood, Squaw, and Soda Springs Ski Resorts, 12-17 inches around Tahoe City, and 8 inches at the Truckee and South Lake Tahoe airports.||In addition to heavy snow and significant travel impacts, widespread wind gusts of 25-35 mph were indicated by mesonet sites with brief gusts to 45 mph for the Truckee and South Lake airports.

This system dumped hefty amounts of snowfall in two increments on the afternoon and evening of the 20th and again during the same period on the 21st. Storm total snowfall included: Mammoth Ski Area with 44 inches, approximately 30 inches for Sonora Pass, Mammoth Ranger Station with 29 inches, and Lee Vining with 21 inches. ||In addition to heavy snow, gusty winds and heavy snow caused near zero visibility and the closure of highways 395 and 167 (just north of Mono Lake) from around 1315PST on the 20th until early morning on the 21st.

Heavy snowfall for this event was mostly above 7000 feet. Mt Rose Ski Area received 18 inches of snowfall while Diamond Peak received 16 inches. Meanwhile, Dagget Pass (7300 ft) only recorded 8 inches and Glenbrook (6350 ft) only saw 2 inches.

Most areas recorded wind gusts of 30-45 mph on the 12th. However, wind-prone and higher elevation sites recorded a brief period of high wind gusts on the morning of the 12th. ||The Galena RAWS (wind-prone) had wind gusts of 68-79 mph from 0400PST to 0700PST. Other higher elevation and wind-prone wind gusts include: Desert Springs RAWS with 58 mph at 0900PST, Washoe Valley with 58-63 mph from 0340PST to 0410PST, Wolf Run Golf Course with 58 mph at 0540PST, and Five Mile Flat NV DOT with 70 at 0325PST.
Most areas has wind gusts of 30-45 mph on the 12th. However, the Walker Lake NV DOT sensor recorded gusts of 59-63 from 0945PST until 1223PST.

Widespread snowfall totals of 10 to 18 inches fell from about 8 miles south of downtown Reno north to near Pyramid Lake, with 4-inch totals as far south as highway 50. The highest amounts fell in the North Valleys of Reno with two feet common.
A general 8 to 12 inches fell from Fallon south and west to Silver Springs (along highway 50) with one report as high as 18 inches near Silver Springs.

A swath of 8 to 12 inches of snow fell from the Sierra Valley north to highway 395 near Honey Lake. The highest amounts were reported along highway 70 from 5 miles west of Beckwourth to near Chilcoot with 18 inches.

Five to 8 inches of snow fell around Yerington while only 0.5 inches fell near Hawthorne.  Besides Yerington, no other reports of heavy snow were reported with the snow band confined to the far northern and western portions of the zone.

For below 6500 feet, 4 to 8 inches of snowfall was reported west of Lake Tahoe with up to 3 inches elsewhere. Snowfall was reduced due to a mix of rain and snow. For areas above 6500-7000 feet widespread 8 to 12 inches of snowfall was reported.

The heaviest snowfall amounts remained west of highway 395 with this storm. Near highway 395, 6 to 9 inches of snowfall was reported around Lee Vining with only 2 inches for Bridgeport. West of highway 395 and above 7000 feet, 10 to 18 inches fell on average with the high end being Mammoth Mountain with 21 inches.
Diamond Peak and Mount Rose Ski Areas received 8 to 12 inches of snowfall. Observations indicate that this event was mostly rain below 6000 to 6500 feet.

This event featured a short period of intense snowfall west of highway 395 with significantly lower amounts from highway 395 east. Here are some snowfall reports: 27 inches at the Mammoth Ski Area, 18 inches at the Mammoth Lakes CO-OP, approximately 14 inches at the Sonora Pass SNOTEL, 5 to 7 inches from Lee Vining south along highway 395 to the Mammoth airport.||In addition to snow, gusty winds of 35-50 mph occurred for portions of highway 395 with a gust to 66 mph at the Walker RAWS.  Over the higher ridges, gusts of 100-125 mph were recorded.

Widespread wind gusts of 35 to 45 mph occurred along with very isolated high wind gusts including 64 mph at the Reno National Weather Service office at 1327PST and 58 mph at the Five Mile Flat NDOT at 1325PST. Wind gusts over the higher ridges (above 8000 feet) ranged from 70-90 mph.

A general 2 to 5 inches of snow fell from Susanville south and west to Portola. Heavy snow criteria was met in a couple isolated spots,  including Portola with 5 inches and the Grizzly Ridge HADS with an estimated 8 inches.

The heaviest accumulations occurred west of Lake Tahoe with 9 to 14 inches while areas below 6500 feet and east of Lake Tahoe only received 2 to 5 inches with some rain mixed in briefly during the afternoon. Here are some specific snowfall totals: 13 inches at the Ward Creek SNOTEL (4 miles WSW Tahoe City), 10 inches for Tahoe City and Donner Memorial State Park, 5 inches at the Truckee airport, and 4 inches at the South Lake Tahoe airport.
Tom's Place reported 4-inch tree limbs down. Here are some specific wind gusts: Mammoth Mountain 122 mph, Mammoth airport AWOS 58 mph, 61 mph at the Walker RAWS, and 60 mph at the Bridgeport RAWS.
A wind gust of 59 mph was reported at the Catnip Mountain RAWS between 1600PST and 1700PST. A dust storm with visibilities below 1/4 mile was reported in Gerlach at 1800PST.

This system produced numerous high wind gusts along with power outages in Dayton, Carson City, and Gardnerville. Here are some specific wind gusts: 72 mph at the Galena RAWS at 1700PST, 66 mph at the Five Mile Flat RAWS at 1600PST, 64 mph at the Wolf Run Golf Course in SW Reno at 1640PST, and 60 mph at the National Weather Service.  In Carson City, strong winds caused difficulty controlling a fire which caused extensive damage to a furniture store (250 to 500k according to fire chief) and a hair salon.

Here are some high wind gusts recorded in the Carson Range east of Lake Tahoe: 71 at the Little Valley RAWS at 0600PST on the 30th, 59 at the Bullseye NDOT sensor at 2200PST, and 58 mph at the Kingbury East Grade NDOT sensor at 1324PST.
High wind gusts were recorded along highway 95 from Schurz to Hawthorne, including 79 mph at the Walker Lake RAWS at 1844PST and 66 mph at the Schurz NDOT sensor at 0155PST on the 30th.
A porch roof was blown off and a skylight broken by strong winds 10 miles south of Winnemucca.

Evidence for a dust storm include widespread wind gusts of 40 to 50 mph and radar and visible satellite images of large amounts of blowing dust coinciding with the timing of lowered visibilities at the Lovelock ASOS. Lovelock had visibilities of 1/4 to 1/2 mile from 1100PST to 1220PST. Other strong wind gusts include: 61 mph at the Pyramid Lake Fisheries at 1730PST and Silver Springs AWOS with 60 mph at 1655PST.

Heavy snow reports for this event include 18 inches at the Mt Rose SNOTEL and 12 inches in Incline Village (spotter). Other reports include 15 inches at the Big Meadow SNOTEL. In addition to snowfall, slick roads caused numerous accidents on highways 50 and 207 (Kingsbury Grade) as well as 2 injuries.

Heavy convective banding caused widespread 6 to 12 inches for the southwestern portion of the forecast zone, generally west of a Fredonyer Pass to Beckwourth to Sierraville Line. Specific snowfall totals include 13 inches in Portola and 6 inches in Sloat. Elsewhere, an estimated 2 to 4 inches fell from near Susanville north to Beiber.

Frequent gusts of 25 to 35 mph (see Truckee and South Lake Tahoe AWOS) accompanied periods of moderate to heavy snowfall with this event. Winds gusted as high as 140 mph over the Sierra crest with as high as 60 mph down to 8000 ft. Some snowfall totals include 20 to 28 inches near the crest, 14 inches in Tahoe City, and 12 inches at the Truckee airport.
Wind gusts averaged 30 to 40 mph with this strong wind event. However, an isolated high wind gust to 60 mph was recorded 3 miles west of Loyalton at 2130PST.

Gusty winds on the 12th included widespread gusts between 35 and 45 mph. However, isolated high wind gusts were reported including 59 mph at the Galena RAWS, 57 mph five miles WSW of Gardnerville, and 58 mph at the Washoe Valley NDOT sensor.

Widespread wind gusts of 40 to 50 mph accompanied a system on the 24th and early on the 25th. However, isolated high wind gusts occurred with 60 mph along highway 50 west of Carson City and 70 mph at the Galena RAWS.

The Mammoth-Yosemite Airport along highway 395 measured high wind gusts on the evening of the 2nd. Other wind gust observations in Mono County include: 145 mph atop Mt. Warren, 109 mph atop Mammoth Mountain, and 62 mph at the Mammoth Base Lodge.
Wind gusts of 64 to 79 mph were reported at the Walker Lake NDOT site along highway 95. The Schurz NDOT sensor reported a gust to 58 mph at 1523PST.

Widespread gusts of 45 to 55 mph were reported with this event, with isolated high wind gusts in wind-prone areas. Virginia Peak recorded a gust to 122 mph. The isolated high wind gusts include: 78 mph at the Galena Creek bridge at 1255PST, 67 mph at the National Weather Service in Reno at 1851PST, and 65 mph at the Washoe Valley NDOT sensor at 1830PST, and 60 mph in NW Reno at 1958PST.||The strong winds (with possible wind shear) caused a Southwest Airlines B737 inbound to the Reno-Tahoe airport (KRNO) to divert to Sacramento. Also, one small plane at KRNO was flipped due to strong winds.

The Carson City based Nevada Appeal relayed a Nevada Highway Patrol report of three accidents (involving 5 vehicles) due to dense fog with visibilities as low as 30 feet and an icy bridge on the Carson City bypass around 0400PST. The dense fog caused the closure of the freeway between 0500PST and 0630PST. In addition to accidents, several flights into the Reno-Tahoe airport were delayed due to the dense fog.

Tahoe Keys (2WSW South Lake Tahoe) recorded this gust at 0234PST. Other high wind reports include a 61 mph gust at the South Lake Tahoe ASOS at 0253PST and sustained winds of 40 to 50 mph at the Lake Tahoe buoys from 0200PST to 0500PST. In addition to high winds reports, trees toppled near South Lake Tahoe and knocked down multiple power lines and a tractor trailer truck was blown over on Interstate 80.

This gust was recorded at the Walker RAWS (2 miles east of highway 395) around 0800PST. Winds gusts over the Sierra ridges reached 115 to 135 mph. Other high wind gusts include 80 mph 4NNW of Lee Vining at 0534PST, 64 mph at the Mammoth-Yosemite airport at 0930PST, and 60 mph at the Bridgeport RAWS at 0804PST.

Winds were sustained at 40 to 50 mph on Lake Tahoe from 0200PST to 0500PST. Slide Mountain recorded a gust to 132 mph. Other high wind gusts include 61 mph at the Little Valley RAWS at 0238PST and 95 mph at the Galena RAWS at 0303PST.

This gust was recorded in southwest Reno near the Arrowcreek Golf Course at 0400PST. The Reno area saw widespread gusts between 60 and 80 mph. Other specific high wind gusts include 107 mph at the Galena Creek Bridge at 0525PST, 81 mph at the Wolf Run Golf Course in southwest Reno, and 70 mph at the National Weather Service Office at 0708PST. ||The exceptionally high winds caused widespread damage, with a Nevada Energy estimate of 5000 homes and businesses without power in the Reno area. Other damage included two trailers blown over on highway 395 in Reno, numerous fences and hundreds of trees uprooted (including a 70 ft pine), as well as many power lines downed. In addition to damage, more than a dozen flights into the Reno-Tahoe airport were canceled due to high winds.
The Hawthorne airport AWOS recorded this gust at 1200PST along with sustained winds of 40 to 50 mph from 1100PST to 1200PST. The Schurz NDOT sensor recorded a gust to 58 mph at 1634PST.

This gust was recorded at the Silver Springs AWOS (along highway 50) at 1235PST. Other high winds gusts include the Lovelock ASOS with 66 mph at 1236PST and the Fallon ASOS with 64 mph at 1341PST. The high winds caused some damage (power lines and trees down and some structural damage) near Fallon. Finally, visibilities of 1/4 mile or less in blowing dust were reported in Lovelock and Fallon by the Nevada Highway Patrol.
A widespread 6 to 10 inch snowfall was reported around the Lake Tahoe Basin, with 10 to 16 inches common west of highway 89 and near the Sierra crest.

Twelve to 18 inches of snowfall fell on average west of highway 395, with the extreme high end being 25 inches at the Mammoth Ski Area. Near and east of highway 395, a general 4 to 8 inches of snow fell including 5 inches in Bridgeport and 8 inches in Lee Vining.

Accumulations for this event were not widespread over the forecast zone, with significant accumulations mainly well west of highway 395 and south of highway 36 with much less snowfall (less than 2 inches) elsewhere. There were some chain controls for the higher terrain of highway 89 in southern Sierra County. Here are some of the higher snowfall totals: 10 inches at the Independence Creek SNOTEL and 7 inches at the Portola CO-OP.

A general 8 to 13 inches of snow fell west of highway 395 near the Sierra crest and in the higher terrain east of highway 395 north of Bridgeport. The exceptions were at the June Lake and Mammoth Mountain Ski areas where 17 to 20 inches were reported. Along and east of highway 395 (except higher terrain north of Bridgeport), much less snowfall occurred with only 2 to 5 inches reported.

Desert Creek flows north out of the Sweetwater Mountains of eastern Mono County. The Desert Creek gauge along the creek indicated a rapid spike to near flood stage between 1900PST and 2200PST. Meanwhile, radar indicated over 2 inches of rainfall. This gauge, the heavy rainfall, and a report of flooding over Desert Creek Road in southern Lyon County indicated likely areas of flash flooding along creeks coming out of the Sweetwater Mountains.

The Lyon County Sheriff Office reported shallow water over Desert Creek Road around 2200PST. However, the Desert Creek stream gauge reported much higher flow (near flood stage) between 2000PST and 2130PST so it is likely that the road was impassable in places previous to the report.

The Bodie CO-OP reported numerous areas of debris flow over state route 270 with some damage along the edges of the road surface. Also, areas of Cottonwood Rd (south of Bodie) were impassable due to flash flooding.
A boat rescue operator on Lake Tahoe reported four 22 to 25 foot boats sunk from Dollar Point (near Tahoe City) south to Rubicon Bay.
This report was from the same thunderstorm that produced the 1655PST gust at the NWS office.
In addition to large hail, the spotter also noted that a friend at the Raley's supermarket at the highways 50 and 89 junction had small dings in their car from the hail.

C/O the Reno Gazette Journal:  The Nevada Highway Patrol indicated that the V and T train derailed near Gold Hill at 1730PST. An official indicated that a mudslide covered the track and caused the derailment. Twelve passengers were on the train but no one was injured. Highway 342 remained closed until around 1145PST on the 9th as the train was put back on its track.

South-southwest to southwest winds on Lake Tahoe were sustained between 20 to 25 mph from late morning to early evening on the 18th. The winds (and waves it generated) were sufficient to sink 3 boats.

Two separate heavy rain events, one on the 4th and one on the 7th, caused ponding of water to more than one foot deep at the Ideal Mobile Home Park.  Other areas of Fallon had periodic standing water and minor flooding, some due to poor drainage.
High winds affected the highway 395 corridor with Bridgeport RAWS and Mammoth AWOS reporting high wind gusts. The highest gust along 395 was 72 mph at the Mammoth AWOS at 1600PST.

Typically windier areas (Washoe Valley, Galena, Five Mile Flat, 5WSW Gardnerville) had high wind gusts since 0600PST on the 24th but more widespread coverage in populated areas did not occur until 1000PST. Here is a list of the highest wind gusts: Galena Creek Bridge 102 mph at 1010PST, Washoe Valley 79 mph at 0610PST with a report of an overturned tractor trailer, Five Mile Flat with 60 mph at 0526PST, and 4SSW of Reno with 61 mph at 1022PST.  In addition to valley/foothills high winds, Virginia Peak and Slide Mountain gusted to between 110 to 130 mph.
Here is a list of noted high wind gusts: Sweetwater NDOT with 78 mph at 1111PST, Walker Lake NDOT with 72 mph at 1505PST, and Schurz NDOT with 58 mph at 1414PST.

Snow with this storm came in two waves, one from the evening of the 19th to the morning of the 20th and the second about 24 hours later. Widespread storm total snowfall of 2 to 3 feet were reported around Lake Tahoe, with local amounts to 4 feet near the crest.  In addition to heavy snow, winds gusted to between 35 and 45 mph especially on the 18th and 19th.

Snowfall with this system fell in two increments, one from the evening of the 19th through the morning of the 20th and the other about 24 hours later. Widespread storm totals of 6 to 12 inches were reported near and west of highway 395 south and west of Susanville, with 15 inches in Portola.

There were 2 main periods of snow with this slow moving storm, with one period from late evening on the 19th to the morning of the 20th and the second period about 24 hours later. Much more snow fell west of highway 395 than along and east, with storm totals of 2.5 to 3.5 feet near the Sierra crest and only 6 to 12 inches along and east of highway 395.  In addition to snowfall, winds were gusting 35 to 50 mph on the 19th with a few gusts over 60 mph from 1400PST to 1700PST for Walker RAWS. Finally, a man was killed near Mammoth Lakes when his vehicle went off a road in low visibility conditions due to heavy snow.

Widespread gusts of 35 to 45 mph occurred on the 18th and 19th ahead of a major winter storm.  Local high wind gusts occurred in wind prone areas, including: 62 at the Washoe Valley NDOT site at 1300PST on the 18th, Galena RAWS with 72 mph at 0300PST on the 19th, and 61 mph at 0600PST on the 18th.

This slow moving storm brought an average of 18 to 30 inches of snowfall in two periods, one from the evening of the 19th to the morning of the 20th and another period about 24 hours later.  In addition to snowfall, gusty winds occurred on the 18th and 19th ahead of the main snowfall with strong ridge winds continuing into the 20th. Local high wind gusts occurred, with 66 mph at Little Valley at 1200PST on the 18th. Meanwhile, Slide Mountain (9650 ft) gusted to 100 mph at 1440PST on the 18th.

Up to 3 inches of snowfall (based on precipitation estimates from Cedarville and Alturas) fell with on the 21st and 22nd with the heaviest amount in the afternoon and evening of the 21st. Isolated higher amounts fell, with Cedarville reporting 5 inches.
A widespread 6 to 8 inches of snow fell in the valleys with 10 to 16 inches near the Sierra crest. In addition to snow, wind gusts of 25 to 35 mph were common on the evening of the 19th.

Widespread wind gusts of 30 to 40 mph occurred, especially from late evening on the 22nd through early morning on the 23rd. Isolated high wind gusts occurred in wind prone areas including: Galena RAWS with 65 mph, Five Mile Flat NDOT and the National Weather Service office with 66 mph, and Washoe Valley NDOT with 62 mph. Two power outages due to downed power lines were reported in the Sparks Tribune.
Widespread gusts of 35 to 45 mph occurred early on the 23rd. Brief and isolated high wind gusts occurred at the Walker Lake RAWS between 0300PST and 0424PST, with a 67 mph gust at 0424PST.

The main brunt of the snowfall with this disturbance was south and west of Susanville. Snowfall totals include: Portola with 4 inches, Grizzly Ridge HADS with an estimated 8 to 12 inches, and and estimated 10 inches at the Independence Creek SNOTEL.

Snowfall totals with this system include: 14 to 20 inches at Squaw Valley and Alpine Meadows Ski areas near the Sierra crest, 16 inches at the South Lake Tahoe Airport, and 12 inches at the Truckee Airport and also at Carnelian Bay on the north side of Lake Tahoe.

A widespread 10 to 16 inches of snow fell in 12 to 14 hours with this system. Gusty winds after the main snowfall caused blowing of snow which made some measurements difficult. Here are some specific snowfall totals: Mt. Rose with an estimated 20 inches, Daggett Pass with 16 inches, Incline Village with 15 inches, and Glenbrook with 10 inches.

Wind gusts were generally between 35 and 45 mph with this system. However,  especially wind prone areas saw gusts over 65 mph, including Galena and Washoe Valley RAWS with 74 mph and 68 mph, respectively, and the National Weather Service in Reno with 66 mph.

Most wind gusts were in the 35 to 50 mph range on the 14th. However, wind prone areas had occasional gusts over 70 mph, including 72 mph at the Sweetwater NDOT at 1000PST and 79 mph at the Walker NDOT at 1844PST. The localized strong winds were sufficient to blow over an empty tractor trailer truck (cross wind) on highway 95 five miles north of Hawthorne, causing two injuries.

Four to 6 inches of snow fell from highway 50 south below 7000 ft with an initial period of rain cutting down accumulations. North of highway 50 as well as above 7000 ft, widespread 10 to 12 inches of snow fell with local amounts to 17 inches above 8000 ft.|In addition to snow, winds gusted between 30 and 40 mph through the afternoon of the 14th, with gusts to 100 mph near ridges.

Rain until around 1400PST cut down snowfall totals to 6 to 8 inches below 7000 ft, with 8 to 12 inches west of Lake Tahoe. Near the crest, 10 to 15 inches of snow fell. In addition to snow, winds gusted to 30 to 45 mph through the afternoon of the 14th, with around 100 mph over the crest.

Three to 6 feet of snow fell above 7000 feet, with 74 inches reported at the Mt Rose Ski Area.  Fifteen to 30 inches fell below 7000 feet with periods of rain to cut down accumulations. In addition to snow, winds gusted to 40 to 55 mph for many areas with gusts as high as 60 to 70 mph on the 19th. Finally, the Mt Rose highway was closed for avalanche control on the 19th.

A widespread 5 to 9 inches of snow fell with this storm before precipitation turned over to rain by 0100PST on the 18th. Local amounts ranged as high as 12 inches north and west of Reno and Carson City. Snow caused nearly 100 accidents, with many during the morning of the 17th. Also, weather caused 4 flight cancellations and 13 delays at the Reno-Tahoe airport.

Widespread gusts of 40 to 50 mph occurred in the late morning and through the afternoon of the 19th. Isolated but brief high winds were also noted in wind prone areas, including 64 mph at the NWS in Reno, 68 mph in Washoe Valley, and 87 mph at the Carson Valley NDOT. A glass table was blown over 5WSW of Gardnerville. Winds gusted to 122 mph over Virginia Pk just southwest of Pyramid Lake.

Areas SW of Susanville received 10 to 20 inches below 7000 feet, with an estimated 2 to 4 feet (based on precip gauges and SNOTELS) above 7000 feet. Elsewhere, much less fell with only up to 6 inches reported. In addition to snow, gusty winds of 30 to 45 mph were widespread on the 19th. A local wind gust to 83 mph was reported just west of Loyalton.

Ski resorts accumulated an average of 5 to 8 feet of snow. Twenty to 30 inches of snow fell north and west of Lake Tahoe below 7000 feet. However, valley areas south and east of Lake Tahoe received as little as 12 inches with periods of rain. Heavy wet snow caused a rock slide on highway 50 which closed the road on the 19th. In addition to snow, numerous reports of downed trees and associated damage were noted on the 19th. Falling trees were responsible for one destroyed house in South Lake Tahoe, with winds gusting to 63 mph and 68 mph in Truckee and South Lake Tahoe, respectively, and up to 155 mph over the crest. Finally, a tree fell on a ski lift cable at the Sierra-at-Tahoe resort and caused skiers to be ejected and injured.

Snowfall totals reached a widespread 5 to 8 feet for the high Sierra, with almost 10 feet for the Mammoth ski area. For elevations below 7500 feet, 1 to 2 feet was reported with some rain at times below 7000 feet. Heavy snow caused the closure of highway 395 on the 19th. As far as winds, widespread wind gusts of 35 to 45 mph were widespread on the 19th, with winds up to 64 mph at the Walker RAWS. For the higher elevations, a 164 mph gust was noted at the  Mammoth ski area chair 1. Strong winds caused some downed trees and power lines in Mammoth Lakes.

Fifteen to 22 inches fell west of Lake Tahoe, mostly within 12 to 15 hours, while 10 to 15 inches for many other areas. In addition to snow, winds gusted to between 30 and 40 mph for many areas with the Sierra crest gusting as high as 109 mph. Some power lines and trees were reported down around Lake Tahoe with 10,000 homes without power for much of the 29th.

Some rain mixed in before 2300PST on the 28th below 8000 feet caused a large range in snow totals, with the highest snowfall totals remaining near the crest and above 8000 ft. Snowfall totals were generally 4 to 8 inches below 8000 feet, increasing to 18 to 30 inches above 8000 feet. Winds gusted 45 to 55 mph for many areas, with gusts as high as 124 mph at the Mammoth ski area.
A widespread 11 to 18 inches of snow fell with this storm. Gusty winds caused some power outages.

Widespread gusts 35 to 50 mph occurred with this system. Isolated high winds gusts were reported, including Washoe Valley with 69 mph, Galena RAWS with 64 mph, and the NWS office with 60 mph. Virginia Peak recorded a gust to 106 mph.
Widespread 35 to 50 mph gusts occurred with this system. Isolated high wind gusts include Walker Lake NDOT, which gusted over 60 mph with a gust to 76 mph at 0024PST on the 29th.

Winds gusted between 60 and 66 mph at the Surprise Valley RAWS the morning of the 14th and then between 65 to 71 mph on the 15th. A few barns and outbuildings were damaged due to winds and power was out from the evening of the 15th to the morning of the 16th. Finally, UPS deliveries were interrupted on the 15th due to the danger of delivery trucks being blown over.
Winds gusted to between 59 and 64 mph (Janesville) on the 15th.  Highway 395 was closed to high profile vehicles between Susanville and the Nevada border for part of the 15th.

Ten to 14 inches of snow fell south and west of Susanville above 4500 feet including Portola and the Sierra Valley. As precipitation began as rain the afternoon of the 15th before changing over to snow the morning of the 16th for areas below 4500 feet only 3 inches was reported in Susanville and 4 inches in Beiber.

Widespread snowfall totals of 1 to 2 feet fell in the Tahoe Basin through the evening of the 16th.  Local snowfall amounts as high as 30 inches were reported near the Sierra crest.  In addition to snowfall, winds gusted as high as 40 mph during the storm.

SNOTEL data and reports from the Mammoth Mountain ski area and spotters indicate that 13 to 18 inches of snow fell near the crest and at higher elevations north of Bridgeport, much of it within 12 hours. Elsewhere, much less snow fell with only 6 to 10 inches of snow near and east of highway 395 from Bridgeport south to near Mammoth Lakes. In addition to snowfall, winds gusted to between 25 and 35 mph during the storm with local areas as high as 50 mph. Meanwhile, the Sierra crest gusted over 130 mph with 156 mph reported at the top of Mammoth Mountain at 0700PST on the 16th.

There was a brief and isolated gust to 66 mph at the Reno Tahoe airport at 0800PST on the 14th but the most widespread high winds occurred on the 15th. Widespread wind gusts of 60 to 67 mph occurred in the foothills and into southern and western areas of Reno from late morning to early afternoon on the 15th. The highest wind gust occurred at the Galena RAWS with 85 mph at 0900PST.  Damage reports with the gusty winds include: an overturned semi truck near Verdi on the 14th, four to 6 inch tree limbs down near Gardnerville on the 15th, a power line down in southwest Reno which sparked a fire (no damage from fire).

Winds gusted between 60 and 84 mph from the evening of the 15th through around 0100PST on the 16th as a cold front moved through the region. The high winds caused highway 95 to be closed between 1800PST on the 15th and 0600PST on the 16th. Specific wind gusts include: 73 mph at the Schurz NDOT station at 2342PST and 84 mph between 1720PST and 1823PST at the Walker Lake NDOT station.

Glenbrook and Daggett Pass CO-OP stations reported 20 to 23 inches of snowfall with this storm, with the Mt Rose ski area receiving over 30 inches. In addition to heavy snow, winds gusted between 35 and 45 mph especially above 6500 feet and on Lake Tahoe.

This period of heavy snow mainly affected areas south and west of Susanville, with an average of 6 to 11 inches in those areas with much less elsewhere (including only one inch in Susanville). The highest snowfall total was reported 3 miles southwest of Susanville with 11 inches.

Snowfall totals from the 17th through the morning of the 19th ranged from 35 to 45 inches near the Sierra crest down to 15 to 25 inches for the Truckee and South Lake Tahoe airports. Here are some specific totals: 31 inches at the Tahoe City CO-OP and 25 inches at the Fallen Leaf (near South Lake Tahoe) and Truckee SNOTELs.

This storm featured two waves, with the first one dropping most of its snow near the crest and north of Bridgeport and the second one hitting most of the county. The first wave dropped 18 to 26 inches near the crest with only a couple inches for Bridgeport and Lee Vining. The second wave dropped an additional 10 to 20 inches near the crest, with 10 to 16 inches for Bridgeport and Lee Vining, and around a foot for Bodie and Crowley Lake.
Daggett Pass CO-OP reported 19 inches with this round of heavy snow, with 30 to 40 inches at the Diamond Peak and Mt Rose ski areas.

A widespread 5 to 8 inches of snow fell for the Reno and Carson City areas, with 8 to 12 inches in the foothills west of highway 395. Lesser amounts of 2 to 4 inches fell east of Reno and Carson City, including Sparks and Spanish Springs.

A widespread 4 to 6 inches of snow fell in about 12 hours. However, with temperatures hovering near freezing there was little impact through around 2000PST on the 18th. Chain and snow tire requirements did become widespread by the morning of the 19th.
Three to 6 inches of snow fell from Susanville south and west, with an 8 inch report from Susanville.
The Cedarville CO-OP observer received 8 inches of snow from this system.

Very hefty snowfall totals were reported especially from Susanville south and west. In that area, a widespread 15 to 30 inches of snow fell with local amounts to 38 inches (5 miles west of Beckwourth). Elsewhere, 8 to 12 inches of snow fell across far northwest Lassen County (around Beiber).

Snowfall totals of 2.5 to nearly four feet were reported at the higher elevations around Lake Tahoe. In the Tahoe Basin, widespread snowfall totals of 14 to 27 inches fell. In addition to heavy snowfall, winds in the Tahoe Basin gusted to between 35 and 45 mph with a gust to 54 mph at 1134PST on the 25th at the Truckee Airport. Over the crest winds were gusting to 90 mph which caused the closure of Squaw Valley and Alpine Meadows ski areas. Finally, an avalanche near Donner Summit caused the closure of Interstate 80 on the 25th.

The bulk of the snow with this event fell west of highway 395. Twenty to 35 inches of snow fell near the crest and at the Mammoth and June Lake ski areas. Elsewhere, 13 inches fell at the Mammoth Ranger Station with an estimated 4 to 8 inches for much of the rest of county. In addition to snow, winds gusted to 35 to 45 mph in many areas with 50 to 60 mph in a few spots along and west of highway 395. Over the ridges, winds gusted as high as 134 mph at the Mammoth Mountain ski area.

Snowfall totals with this event include: 17 inches at Glenbrook (near Lake Tahoe) with 25 to 35 inches for Daggett Pass north to Incline Village and the Mt Rose ski area. In addition to snow, winds gusted over 40 mph for many areas from late morning through the afternoon on the 25th with gusts over 50 mph for a few locations including the Glenbrook Canyon NDOT station and the Little Valley RAWS. Over ridges, winds gusted over 80 mph with gusts as high as 110 mph for Slide Mountain.
Five inches of snow was reported in Gerlach with this system.

Widespread snowfall totals of 5 to 10 inches fell during this system, with 12 to 18 inches in areas west of Carson City and south and west of Reno (possibly enhanced by lake effect snow from Lake Tahoe). In addition to snow, winds gusted over 50 mph in the foothills and south of Reno from late morning into the afternoon on the 25th. Winds and snow in the Carson Valley caused 24 power poles to be broken or fall down onto both highway 395 and Muller Lane. In addition, several accidents caused at least two injuries in the Carson Valley. Finally, the snow was enough to cause Governor Sandoval to send home early non-essential state workers on the 25th.
Widespread wind gusts of 40 to 50 mph were measured on the 10th. An isolated high wind gust to 61 mph was recorded at the Surprise Valley RAWS at 0830PST.

Widespread wind gusts of 45 to 55 mph occurred on the 10th. A few high wind gusts occurred as well, including: the National Weather Service in Reno as well as the Galena RAWS with 70 mph at 1000PST, Desert Springs RAWS with 63 mph at 1400PST, 65 mph at 1050PST at the Wolf Run Golf Course, and 60 mph at the Reno-Tahoe airport at 1200PST.  Gusty winds caused the closure of highway 395 through the Washoe Valley in the evening. Meanwhile, wind gusts of 100 to 120 mph at Slide Mountain and Virginia Peak were recorded.

Widespread wind gusts of 45 to 55 mph were recorded on the 10th. A few high wind gusts occurred as well, including 61 mph at the Sweetwater NDOT site at 1900PST and 77 mph at the Walker Lake NDOT sensor at 1800PST. High winds at Walker Lake lasted no longer than an hour, but they caused the closure of highway 95 between Schurz and Luning (Mineral County).

Widespread wind gusts of 40 to 50 mph occurred with this system. However, there were brief high winds in wind prone areas including the Walker Lake NDOT sensor with gusts of 66 to 77 mph and the Sweetwater NDOT sensor with gusts between 60 and 69 mph between 2000PST and 2200PST.

A widespread snowfall of 10 to 20 inches was reported above 6500 feet with this system, with isolated amounts of 20 to 28 inches near the Sierra crest. Below 6500 feet, only 2 to 5 inches was reported as much of the precipitation was rain. The exception was on the west side of Lake Tahoe with the Tahoe City CO-OP reporting 9 inches.  Highways 89 and 50 were closed for a time on the 16th for avalanche control.

Fourteen to 21 inches of snow fell on the 15th and 16th north of highway 50 above 6500 feet with lesser amounts further south. Below 6500 feet, up to 5 inches of snow fell with much of the precipitation falling as rain. Here are some specific snowfall totals: Incline Village with 14 inches, the Mount Rose Ski area with 21 inches, Daggett Pass with 11 inches, and Glenbrook with 5 inches.

Seven inches of snow fell in Susanville while 13 inches fell in Portola on the 18th and early on the 19th.  An estimated 16 inches of snow fell in extreme southern Sierra County at the Independence Camp SNOTEL.

Widespread snowfall totals of 1 to 2 feet were reported from the afternoon of the 18th to the morning of the 19th. Locally higher amounts include: an estimated 30 to 40 inches of snow at the Boreal and Squaw Valley ski areas and 27 inches at Tahoma.

Widespread wind gusts of 45 to 55 mph occurred on the 18th. However, isolated high wind gusts were reported at NDOT sensors, including: 66 mph near Walker Lake, 60 mph at Sweetwater, and 58 mph at Schurz.
Widespread wind gusts of 45 to 55 mph occurred on the 18th. A few areas saw high wind gusts, including: 76 mph at the Galena RAWS, 65 mph in NW Reno, and 62 mph at the Reno-Tahoe airport.

Widespread wind gusts of 40 to 50 mph occurred on the 18th. Brief high wind gusts also occurred in Silver Springs, with gusts over 60 mph between 1100PST and 1200PST with the highest being 67 mph at 1135PST.  A large tree was knocked down onto power lines in Fallon.

Most of the heavy snowfall in this period fell over Plumas and Sierra Counties near the crest with much less further north and east. Snowfall totals include 15 to 20 inches at the Independence Creek and Camp SNOTELS, 8 inches in Portola, and 2 to 5 inches elsewhere.

Widespread snowfall totals of 12 to 18 inches fell on the 20th, including 14 inches in South Lake Tahoe and 13 inches in Tahoe City. In addition to snowfall, heavy snow and wind conspired to bring periods of near zero visibility to Interstate 80 near Truckee which caused its closure. In addition, avalanche control caused the closure of highways 50, 88, and 89 which resulted in major travel delays.
Twenty-two to 32 inches of snow fell on the 20th and into early on the 21st in the higher elevations and near Lee Vining (22 inches), with 12 to 18 inches elsewhere.
A widespread 10 to 20 inches of snow fell on the 20th, with most of the snow falling in a 12 to 15 hour period.

Two rounds of snowfall occurred from the 23rd through the evening of the 24th. The first round dropped a light snowfall, mainly above 5000 ft, while the second round dropped widespread snowfall totals of 10 to 20 inches from Susanville south, with the highest amounts near Portola and the Sierra Valley.

Two rounds of snow occurred during this storm, the first on the 23rd and the stronger second round on the 24th. The first round dropped the heaviest snow near the crest where 12 to 20 inches of snow was reported, with other areas only receiving 3 to 6 inches. The second round dropped 2 to 4 feet above 7000 feet and 1 to 2 feet elsewhere.  In addition to snowfall, gusty winds with the second round of snow caused low visibilities and the closure of Interstate 80 from Truckee to Colfax. Also, highway 89 was closed for avalanche control on the 24th.

Two rounds of snow occurred from the 23rd through early morning on the 25th. The first round affected areas mostly west of highway 395, with 18 to 34 inches of snowfall near the crest but only 4 to 6 inches near Lee Vining. The second round affected a larger area with heavy snowfall, including 8 to 14 inches around Lee Vining and 2 feet at the Mammoth Lakes Ranger Station. In addition to snowfall, gusty winds of 25 to 35 mph affected much of the area with up to 116 mph over the crest.

Two rounds of snow occurred with this storm, the first on the 23rd and the second from midday on the 24th through late evening on the 24th. The first round only dropped 4 to 8 inches of snow, however the second round dropped one to two feet. In addition to snowfall, gust winds of 25 to 35 mph accompanied the second round of snow on the 24th.

A band of snow stalled out between Fallon and Reno bringing several inches of wet snowfall, with a narrow band of 4 to 8 inches from just west of Fallon to near Silver Springs. Here are some specific totals: 7 to 8.5 inches in Silver Springs, 4 inches in Fernley, and 2 inches in Fallon.

A band of snow stalled out between Fallon and Reno bringing several inches of wet snowfall to Lyon County. The Mason Valley news reported up to 5 inches of snow in the Mason Valley while a CoCORAHS report 3 miles SSW of Yerington reported 3.5 inches.

Widespread wind gusts of 45 to 55 mph occurred on the 26th. Isolated high wind gusts also occurred in wind prone areas, including: 75 mph at the Washoe Valley NDOT site, 69 mph in NW Reno and at the National Weather Service, 63 mph at the Black Springs NDOT site, and 60 mph 3 miles ESE of Carson City.

Widespread gusts of 40 to 50 mph occurred on the 26th. Isolated high winds were also reported, including 72 and 61 mph at the Walker Lake and Sweetwater NDOT sites, respectively. According to the Mineral County Independent News, the gusty winds near Walker Lake caused a semi truck to overturn and a house boat to be blown off its trailer and crushed.

Winds gusted over 58 mph the evening of the 6th into early morning on the 7th at the Walker Lake NDOT site. Wind gusts reached 70 to 97 mph between 2000PST and 0100PST, with the 97 mph gust at 2230PST. In addition to Walker Lake, the Sweetwater NDOT site gusted to 71 mph.

Widespread wind gusts of 40 to 50 mph occurred on the 25th. Isolated high winds also were noted in wind prone areas, including 60 mph at the Washoe Valley NDOT site, 59 mph in southwest Reno at the Wolf Run Golf Course, and 58 mph at the Galena RAWS. In addition to gusty winds, a report of minor wind damage to a roof in Carson City was reported.

Widespread wind gusts of 40 to 50 mph occurred on the 6th. Isolated high wind gusts also occurred in wind prone areas, including 59 mph at the Washoe Valley NDOT site and gusts 74 to 89 mph between 0100PST and 0300 PST at the Galena RAWS.

Four to seven inches of snow fell from South Lake Tahoe north and west to the Sierra crest near Donner Summit. The morning snow and cold as well as wet roads later in the day forced the delay and eventual cancellation of the first leg of the Amgen Pro Cycling Tour.

Widespread wind gusts of 40 to 50 mph accompanied this system. Isolated high winds also occurred, with the wind prone Walker Lake NDOT sensor recording gusts between 60 and 75 mph with a gust to 80 mph at 0643PST.

Widespread sustained winds of 30 to 45 mph occurred on the 25th. The highest wind gusts noted include 64 mph and 80 mph at the Schurz and Sweetwater NDOT sensors, respectively, and 71 mph in the Smith Valley.

Widespread wind gusts of 45 to 55 mph occurred on the 25th. A few high winds also occurred, including 64 mph at the Washoe Valley NDOT site, 63 mph in northwest Reno, and 60 mph at the Carson Valley NDOT site and at the Western Nevada Community College on the west side of Carson City. Strong winds caused a tree to fall over onto a power line in Sparks. In Wadsworth, winds blew power lines together which caused two small fires with some building damage and an injury to a firefighter.

Widespread sustained winds of 30 to 40 mph with gusts 45 to 55 mph occurred on the afternoon and early evening of the 25th. A few areas of high winds were also noted, including sustained winds of 40 to 50 mph with gusts as high as 66 mph for the Lovelock ASOS, gusts to 65 mph for the Dead Camel Mountain RAWS, and sustained winds of 40 to 52 mph with gusts to 64 mph for the Silver Springs AWOS.

Wind gusts between 60 and 70 mph near the highway 395 corridor on the 25th. Specific high wind gusts include 73 mph at the Walker RAWS, 66 mph at the Mammoth airport AWOS, and 60 mph on the west side of Mammoth Lakes. Winds over Mammoth Mountain gusted between 100 and 140 mph.

High winds during the afternoon and early evening of the 31st caused at least two semi trucks to overturn on highway 395 between Mono Lake and Crowley Lake. Winds also blew the roof off the Upside Down House in Lee Vining. The roof landed against the Old Schoolhouse Museum and broke through one wall of the museum. Here are some specific wind gusts: Lee Vining with 80 mph, Crowley Lake with 75 mph, Walker RAWS with 71 mph, Bridgeport RAWS with 65 mph, and the Mammoth airport AWOS with 64 mph.
Widespread wind gusts of 40 to 50 mph occurred on the 31st. However, a wind prone area 5 miles WSW of Gardnerville reported gusts between 66 and 73 mph with minor roof damage (shingles torn off).
The intersection of Whiskey Springs and Grass Valley Road had about a foot of water flowing over it. Standing water was also reported on other roads in the area.

The Lower Lee Vining, Moraine, Aspen, and Big Bend campgrounds are partially or completely closed due to snowmelt flooding from Lee Vining Creek. Monetary damages due to loss of income from the closed campsites and one culvert was washed out leading to higher water in campgrounds.

California Land Management indicated that the Twin Lakes Campground (30 campsites) was completely shut down due to snowmelt flooding. No damage to campground property noted just the loss of income from the closed campsites.
A bridge crossing McGee Creek was destroyed by flood waters. The location of the washed out bridge is approximate.
Deadman campground closed due to flooding along Deadman Creek. No damage to campground property noted just the loss of income from the closed campsites.
Heavy snowmelt caused minor to moderate lowland flooding late in June and into early July in the Mason Valley south of Yerington with some backyards and crop fields flooded.

The Modoc County Record reported that strong winds came down from Cedar Pass and snapped a 30-inch and a 16-inch diameter tree near Cedarville. A building on one ranch had a 20 foot by 34 foot piece of roof blown off. Large farm equipment (swather) was pushed and numerous 110 pound bales of hay were rolled or knocked over in the winds.|The highest measured gust was 55 mph at the Surprise Valley RAWS.

Lyon County Emergency Management reported a significant amount of water over East Walker and Pine Grove Roads with one truck in water up to the bottom of its cab. The deepest water was in the area of the Flying M Ranch.

The Mono County sheriff reported a 1/4 to 1/2 mile wide landslide over highway 395 in the Walker River Canyon that closed the road between Walker and Sonora Junction (highway 108). The slide was up to 5 feet deep and closed the highway for a couple hours.

Lightning from a thunderstorm over the McQueen High School soccer field struck between two sets of bleacher seats on the afternoon of the 24th, causing 4 injuries. Two of the injured went to the hospital and were in stable condition while two others refused treatment. One man had his hair singed and the left half of his shirt burned.
A spotter in Stagecoach measured a thunderstorm wind gust to 70 mph which caused a power outage and possibly the breaking of a utility pole.
Heavy rain also accompanied the hail.
Very heavy rainfall also accompanied the hail.

Snowfall estimates from SNOTEL sites and CoCoRAHS indicated an average of 6 to 12 inches of snow fell above 7000 feet from the evening of the 4th through the morning of the 5th, with mainly rain for the Tahoe Basin. Precipitation amounts ranged from around 0.75 inches to 1.5 inches, highest near the crest.
Six to 12 inches of snow fell above 8000 feet with this system, with up to 3 inches down to 7500 feet. This caused passes over the Sierra crest to be closed temporarily.

The Mt Rose SNOTEL had an estimated 12 of snow from late on the 4th through mid morning on the 5th. Further south and east, amounts were considerably less with an estimated 3-6 for Daggett Pass (CO-OP) and Big Meadow (SNOTEL). The snow level for the bulk of the precipitation event remained between 7000 and 7500 feet.

As low pressure settled over the region, widespread snow showers dropped another 2 to 6 inches of snow (highest amounts near the crest). Local snowfall amounts of 7 to 12 inches were indicated near the crest per SNOTEL and CoCoRAHS data.

Widespread snowfall totals of 2 to 4 inches fell across eastern Plumas, Sierra, and extreme southern Lassen Counties on the 3rd and early on the 4th. However, a narrow band of heavy snow developed late in the evening of the 3rd and dropped 9 to 13 inches in the Portola and Graeagle areas.

High winds started in the foothills late on the evening of the 17th, with high wind gusts becoming widespread over the rest of the area early on the morning of the 18th. Here are some of the highest gusts: 80 mph at the highways 50 and 395 junction in south Carson City, 79 mph at the National Weather Service, and 71 mph at the Wolf Run Golf course in southwest Reno. High winds caused the arcing of power lines which started the Caughlin Fire just after midnight on the 18th.

Winds gusted between 59 and 69 mph from Sweetwater Summit in far southern Lyon County north into the Mason and Smith Valleys (including Yerington). The strongest winds were along highway 95 near Walker Lake, where winds gusted between 80 and 94 mph from 1340PST and 1800PST. A number of trees were reported down in Lyon County, with a blown transformer with power outages in Wellington and Silver Springs.

Widespread gusts between 70 and 91 mph were reported on the 18th, mainly south of Bridgeport. Some higher gusts include: 91 mph 4NNW Lee Vining (gap wind), 86 mph at the Mammoth-Yosemite airport, and 70 mph at the Walker RAWS. High winds caused a downed power pole which closed highway 395 in Walker while a tractor trailer truck was blown into a ditch near the intersection of highways 395 and 167.

High winds caused a tree to fall on a power line sparking a rapidly spreading wildfire in southwest Reno around 0030PST. The 2,000 acre Caughlin Fire fire spread, sometimes up to 30 mph, and caused the destruction of around 30 homes during the early morning of the 18th. Over 9,000 people were evacuated from the fire area early Friday before being allowed to return Saturday. One man died while evacuating his home, a firefighter suffered second-degree burns, and 16 others were admitted to area hospitals for smoke inhalation.

Widespread winds gusting to between 40 and 50 mph from the east and northeast caused numerous trees to fall across power lines and into a few residences in South Lake Tahoe, especially near Pioneer Trail Blvd. (where trees were reported in the road). In addition, strong winds generated waves to several feet on Lake Tahoe which caused extensive damage to the Camp Richardson dock in South Lake Tahoe.

Elevations below 8500 feet gusted between 40 and 52 mph on the 1st. However, winds above 8500 to 9000 feet near the crest blew much stronger with sustained winds of 50 to 80 mph with gusts of at least 135 to 155 mph (top wind gust of 154 mph recorded). Most of the damage from winds was near the Mammoth Lakes Pack Station (Madera County) where the U.S. Forest Service reported that several hundred trees were blown down. See Storm Data from the National Weather Service in Hanford for more information.

A Sierra Avalanche Center report indicated that three skiers were skiing in the backcountry near Alpine Meadows when one of the skiers triggered an avalanche about 300 ft wide by 500 feet long and one foot deep. The skier was buried under 3 feet of snow. The other two skiers found the victim within several minutes. However, the victim sustained severe injuries due to impact with trees and debris and died in the hospital that night.

Winds gusted between 60 and 84 mph for areas along and west of highway 395 from Reno south into the Carson Valley on the 19th. The highest winds were in and near the foothills south of Reno with 78 mph at the Galena RAWS and 84 mph at the Washoe Valley NDOT sensor. Strong winds were responsible for a blown over tractor trailer along highway 395 near Red Rock Road (north valleys of Reno) which caused 3 injuries, damage to 13 vehicles, and the shutting down of highway 395.

Strong winds (up to 84 mph) and the improper disposal of fireplace ashes caused the rapid spread of a fire originating at the north end of Washoe Valley early in the afternoon on the 19th. Thousands of people were forced to evacuate from the swift-moving fire. Around 3100 acres were burned with 28 homes destroyed (7 damaged) and one fatality attributed to the fire. ||For information purposes only (not direct costs from wildfire), the tally of fire-fighting related costs were at least 1.5 million dollars.

Snow levels surged to 8500 to 9000 feet during the evening of the 20th before falling to valley floors by the morning of the 21st. This limited the snowfall totals to 6 inches or less below 7000 feet while areas above 8000 feet received 10-20 inches of heavy wet snow. Overall liquid precipitation of 2 to 4 inches fell with this very wet storm.

Heavy snowfall on the 20th and 21st was generally limited to areas above 8000 feet due to a relatively warm airmass during the period of heaviest precipitation. Snowfall totals ranged from 10 to 20 inches above 8000-8500 feet to 3 inches or less below 7500 ft.

This heavy, wet snow event dropped 1 to 2 feet of snow near the crest with 10 to 17 inches below 7000 feet north and west of Lake Tahoe. For areas near Lake Tahoe level (including Truckee and South Lake Tahoe), an average 5 to 7 inches of snow fell.

This event brought 1 to 2 feet of snow near the crest with as much as a foot above 7500-8000 feet east of highway 395 and north of Mono Lake. Elsewhere, much less snow fell with 7 to 8 inches for the Lee Vining area but generally less than 4 inches elsewhere.

Precipitation started as rain below 7500 feet on the evening of the 20th, therefore the heaviest snowfall remained at the higher elevations. Snowfall totals include 21 inches at the Mount Rose Ski area and 12 inches near Incline Village but only 4 to 6 inches at the Diamond Peak Ski area and 2 inches in Glenbrook. Overall liquid precipitation totals of 1.5 to 3 inches fell in this very wet storm.

This system brought more significant snowfall to areas below 6500-7000 feet as compared with the system on the 20th and 21st. Snowfall totals include 19 to 23 inches at the Mount Rose Ski area, 20 inches in Incline Village, 14 inches at Daggett Pass, and 5 inches in Glenbrook.

The best accumulations with this event fell south of Susanville per radar and precipitation gauge reports. Four to 8 inches of snow fell near and below 5000 feet west of highway 395 with 11 inches at the Independence Creek SNOTEL (6500 feet elevation).
On the 27th, 5 to 8 inches of snow fell in the lower elevations of the Lake Tahoe Basin while 10 to 15 inches of snow fell along and near the Sierra crest.
Widespread snowfall totals of 6 to 9 inches fell with this system, with local amounts of 12 to 17 inches near the Mount Rose and Sky Tavern ski areas.

A widespread snowfall of 5 to 10 inches fell west of highway 395 (locally up to a foot) with up to several inches east of highway 395. Here are some more specific snowfall totals: 3 SSW Susanville (CoCoRAHS) with 12 inches, 8 inches at the Susanville CO-OP, and 5 to 7 inches along highway 70/89 between Blairsden and Sloat. In addition to heavy snowfall, widespread gusty winds of 35-45 mph occurred with local gusts as high as 64 mph along highway 395 south of Susanville.

One to two feet of snow fell along and west of highway 89 with 6 to 12 inches in South Lake Tahoe and east of the Truckee airport with this storm. The bulk of the snow fell on the morning of the 29th. In addition to snow, gusty winds of 35-45 mph (with a gust to 53 mph at the South Lake Tahoe airport at 1253PST) accompanied the storm.
Three inches of snow fell in Cedarville during the morning of the 29th, with localized amounts of 3 to 6 inches reported by spotters a few miles north of Cedarville.

Ten to 20 inches of snow fell with this system from Incline Village to Mount Rose, with considerably less snowfall from Marlette Lake south (up to 8 inches). In addition to snowfall, gusty winds of 35-45 mph occurred on the 29th with local gusts 58-62 mph from Glenbrook Canyon to Little Valley.

Widespread wind gusts of 59 to 71 mph occurred on the 29th in and south of the Mason and Smith Valleys, with the highest winds over Sweetwater (hwy 338) and Anchorite (hwy 359) Summits. However, the highest winds in the area occurred along hwy 95 near Walker Lake where winds gusted between 75 and 89 mph between 0800PST and 1100PST.

Widespread wind gusts of 45 to 55 mph were recorded on March 1st. However, winds gusted between 60 - 72 mph at the Mammoth airport (AWOS) between 0730PST and 0900PST. Winds gusted over 100 mph at Mammoth Mountain above 9500 feet.
The Surprise Valley RAWS reported winds gusting to between 68 and 73 mph.

Widespread wind gusts between 40 and 50 mph were reported on the 13th. However, local areas along highway 395 just south of Janesville recorded winds gusts up to 65 mph with 2 tractor trailer trucks and several trees blown over/down.

Areas of heavy snow fell near the Sierra crest with much less snowfall elsewhere along and west of highway 89 on the 13th and 14th. East of highway 89, very little snow fell during the same period with rain or a mixture of rain and snow below 7000 feet limiting accumulations. Snowfall totals include: 12-20 inches (locally 2 feet) near the crest with 6-8 inches elsewhere near and west of highway 89. An additional 3-8 inches of snow fell near the crest on the morning of the 15th.

Widespread winds of 25 to 35 mph with gusts to 55 mph were recorded on the 13th. However, localized areas saw stronger winds, including the Reno-Tahoe airport with sustained winds of 40-44 mph with gusts up to 59 mph, Galena RAWS with gusts 60-70 mph (as high as 80 mph 0800-0900PST), and Washoe Valley with gusts up to 68 mph.

An estimated 12 to 16 inches of snow fell in the higher terrain of eastern Plumas and Sierra Counties with this system. Below 5000 feet, little snowfall was noted except in the Feather River Basin along highways 70 and 89. This includes 4 inches in Portola.

Eighteen to 36 inches of snow fell for ski areas west of highway 89 on the 16th and 17th, with local amounts of 3 to 4 feet near the crest. Elsewhere, the main snowfall fell overnight from the 16th into the 17th with a widespread 8 to 13 inches reported per SNOTEL and CO-OP data.

An estimated 12 to 20 inches of snow fell west of highway 395 (except 20-24 inches Mammoth Lakes and 39 inches Mammoth Mountain Ski area) from the evening of the 16th through early morning on the 17th. Elsewhere, 10-12 inches fell in Lee Vining with 6 inches for Bodie and Tom's Place. Meanwhile, Bridgeport only saw a very light accumulation (specific amounts missing).

Eighteen to 24 inches of snow fell near Diamond Peak ski area with 22 to 32 inches from Incline Village (above 7000-7500 ft) to the Mount Rose Ski area. Below 7000 feet, most snow fell from the evening of the 16th through the early morning of the 17th including 10 inches at Glenbrook and 12 inches at Incline Village (at 6700 ft).

Widespread wind gusts of 40 to 50 mph occurred with this system. However, much stronger local wind gusts occurred between 2100PST on the 16th through 0100PST on the 17th, including gusts over 60 mph (briefly 74-95 mph between 2300-2400PST) at the Walker Lake NDOT sensor.

Snow and lower elevation rain changed to a heavy, wet snow early in the afternoon on the 31st. This brought a widespread 3-6 inches of snowfall to areas below 6000 feet, with 6-10 inches above 6000 feet. Locally higher amounts were reported, including 9 2W Blairsden.
