Eight to 13 inches of snow fell on the west side of Lake Tahoe while ski areas received 12 to 18 inches of snowfall. Meanwhile, areas east of highway 89 only received 4 to 8 inches of snow although much of the snow was in a 4-hr period (heavy snowfall rate).

Winds were sustained at 40-50 mph on Lake Tahoe during the morning of the 31st. According to the Coast Guard, these winds generated 4-foot waves on the north shore of the lake. The Truckee Airport reported sustained winds of 35-45 mph with gusts between 58-70 mph. Elsewhere, widespread gusts 40-50 mph were reported.

High winds were reported along highway 395 north of Bridgeport with gusts 61-76 mph at the Walker RAWS and gusts up to 64 mph at the Bridgeport RAWS. High winds also may have occurred east of Mono Lake as winds were gusting 70-75 mph at Brawley Peak and along highway 359 just over the state line in Nevada.

Widespread gusts of 35-45 mph were reported with this system. However, winds were locally higher with sustained winds of 40-50 mph (for one hour) on Lake Tahoe and local gusts up to 65 mph (up to 76 over ridges) in the Carson Range. Winds up to 4 feet were noted on Lake Tahoe on the north shore of Lake Tahoe in California.

Sustained winds over 40 mph with gusts 58-64 mph were reported at the Reno-Tahoe airport, the National Weather Service in Reno, and in Palomino Valley (southwest of Pyramid Lake). Gusts to 66 mph occurred at the Reno-Stead airport with gusts over 60 mph along highway 395 in the Carson and Washoe Valleys. Winds over Virginia Peak gusted to 106 mph.

Winds on the 31st were sustained between 35 and 47 mph with gusts 60-64 mph at the Fallon and Lovelock ASOS sites and at the Humboldt House NDOT site. Elsewhere, widespread gusts over 50 mph (and 61 mph at the Silver Springs AWOS) occurred on the 31st. Strong winds caused blowing dust which reduced visibility to 1/4 mile or less at times in Lovelock and Fallon. In addition, a window was reported broken by the wind (not debris) in Lovelock and a single-wide trailer was blown over near Rye Patch Reservoir.

Sustained winds on the 31st reached 40-47 mph with gusts 65-70 mph from Anchorite Summit (hwy 359) to Yerington with gusts as high as 69 mph along hwy 95 near Schurz. The Walker Lake NDOT sensor had a 76 mph gust at 1330PST. NDOT reported a dust storm which closed hwy 95 from Hawthorne to Luning late in the afternoon. Finally, the Yerington sheriff's office reported power lines and 2 telephone poles down, 3 transformers on fire, and the entire town without power at 1530PST.
Spotter estimated nickel size hail in Janesville.
This wind gust was measured at the Blue Door RAWS.
This gust was measured at the Bluewing Mt RAWS.
The Naval Air Station in Fallon reported this wind gust. Sustained winds were 41 mph at 1452PST.
This wind gust was measured by the Surprise Valley RAWS.
A spotter 3 miles north of Cedarville reported a foot of snow, with as much as 2 feet of snow reported in Lake City.
The El Dorado County sheriff reported several trees down near the Lake Tahoe Golf Course between 1400-1445PST. The trees caused damage to homes and cars.

A spotter reported some damage to metal roofs in Mammoth Lakes. Widespread wind gusts of 45-55 mph were recorded on the 26th. However, the Mammoth Airport reported brief gusts as high as 63 mph. Over Mammoth Mountain, winds gusted well over 100 mph with gusts between 125-150 mph above 9500 feet.
The Pyramid Lake Fisheries observation in Sutcliffe reported this wind gust.

An open residential burn in the Topaz Ranch Estates (a couple miles north of Topaz Lake) the previous weekend re-ignited as winds gusted to 40-45 mph on the afternoon of the 22nd. The fire claimed several cars, as well as 19 structures including 2 homes. The total acreage of the fire was 7152. Fire fighting costs (not fire damage) reached more than 3 million dollars.

Sustained winds between 41 and 53 mph with gust up to 64 mph were reported at the Schurz NDOT site and Hawthorne AWOS. In addition, a few trees and power lines were downed in Yerington along with visibility down to 100 yds.  In Hawthorne, visibility was down to 1/2 mile at the airport. Fourteen miles south of Walker Lake along highway 95, low visibility was deemed responsible for a 3 car pile and the closure of the highway between Fallon and Luning.

The Silver Springs AWOS and Stagecoach NDOT site indicated winds sustained between 40 and 55 mph with gusts 66 to 69 mph on the afternoon of the 4th. Dead Camel RAWS (18 miles SW of Fallon) had winds sustained up to 42 mph with gusts to 60 mph. Several trees were down on roads with a total of 16-20 trees downed around Fernley. Also, some fences were downed and power out along with visibility down to 1/2 mile in Fernley.

A Reno news station meteorologist and a couple spotters sent several videos of fast flowing water over Nye Road near its intersection with Johnson Lane. The water caused severe damage to Nye Road. The water was also seen flowing down Johnson Lane closer to highway 395. The Douglas County Sheriff reported water flowing over multiple roads in the Minden-Johnson Lane area around 1720PST.
The Mineral County Fire Department reported a debris flow across highway 95 which caused some road damage.

A 71-yr-old man was struck and killed by lightning during an early morning thunderstorm at Donner Memorial State Park just west of Truckee, CA.  He had been camping with family in the Park and was outside in an area of tall trees.
A sensor west of Ragtown near highway 50 reported gusts to 77 mph.
Thunderstorm winds caused a 4 to 5 foot diameter tree to fall on St. Clair Street in Fallon.

Very large amounts of pea to marble size hail (with some hail as large as nickels) from a slow-moving thunderstorm caused around 4 inches of accumulating hail.  The hail depth was directly verified by a National Weather Service employee.  The hail caused a number of residential gardens to be damaged or destroyed.

Large rocks and mud covered highway 395 near the Ray May burn scar as heavy rain caused the hillside to give way. The debris flow/rock slide caused highway 395 to be closed as heavy equipment was required to remove the rocks from the road.
An estimated 10 to 20 inches of snow fell on the 22nd and early on the 23rd.

Most snow with this system fell west and south of Susanville to the west of highway 395. An estimated 12 to 18 inches of snow fell at the higher elevations of Plumas County. At the lower elevation, 3 to 6 inches fell in Portola and Sierraville (and possibly several inches of wet snow in Beiber).
This storm brought 8 to 14 inches of snow north and west of Lake Tahoe with 14 to 22 inches west of highway 89 above 6500 feet.

A band of heavy snow developed between highway 36 to the north and just north of Portola to the south. The band extended as far east as Susanville and Janesville along highway 395. Snowfall in this band averaged 5 to 9 inches with up to 18 inches near Janesville.

Four to 7 inches (locally to 9) of snow fell in a narrow lake effect snow band extending from Lake Tahoe to near or just west-northwest of Carson City. Lesser amounts of 1 to 3 inches fell between Carson City and Minden.

Wind gusts of 76 and 85 mph were reported in Janesville and along highway 395 near Sears Road (respectively) on the morning of the 21st. The high winds caused the closure of highway 395 from the Nevada state line to Johnstonville. In addition, a power outage and metal roof damage were reported 4 miles ESE Janesville.

This event brought mostly rain or a mix of rain and snow to the Lake Tahoe area below 7500 feet. Above 7500 feet, 10 to 18 inches of snow fell with 17 to 27 inches above 8500 feet per SNOTEL estimates and Sierra Avalanche Center observations.

Most snowfall was restricted to above 7500 feet north of Bridgeport and west of highway 395 (near the crest) with this storm. The Mammoth Ranger Station reported 11 inches of snowfall, while SNOTEL estimates above 8500 feet ranged from 12 to 20 inches with local amounts of 24 to 30 inches. The main Sierra passes were already closed for winter so little cross-Sierra traffic impact was noted.

Winds gusted between 68 and 90 mph in the foothills with the strongest winds in the Galena area where a 20-second sustained wind speed of 90 mph was reported by a spotter. Over Virginia Peak (SW of Pyramid Lake), winds gusted as high as 127 mph. In the Reno area, winds gusted to 67 mph at the National Weather Service office, 62 mph in West Reno, and 59 mph at the Reno-Tahoe airport. Damage to a hangar at the Reno airport was noted around 0300PST on the 30th.

Winds gusted between 35 and 45 mph on the 29th into the morning of the 30th. However, locally higher gusts were reported including 53 in Smith Valley and between 71 and 88 mph at the Walker Lake RAWS near Hawthorne.

Snow levels remained fairly high during this event with only up to 4 inches down to 6800 feet. However, at Daggett Pass (7334 feet) 8 inches was reported with amounts of 17 to 23 inches above 8000 feet.
The Surprise RAWS reported winds gusting to between 65 and 90 mph.
Wind gusts between 62 and 87 mph were indicated by the Pierce RAWS with 63 mph at the Rice Canyon RAWS. Meanwhile, along highway 395 winds gusted as high as 70 mph (Doyle RAWS).

High winds and localized damage were reported from Lee Vining northward on the 2nd. Winds gusted between 60 and 75 at the Walker RAWS and between 59 and 62 at the Bridgeport RAWS and in Lee Vining. Broken tree branches were noted in Lee Vining while shingles were torn from the roof of several buildings. At the higher elevations of Mammoth Mountain, winds gusted to around 150 mph.
The California Highway Patrol reported boulders the size of a motor cycle on Frenchman Lake Road.
Mudslide on highway 70 between Blairsden and Portola.  A 24-hr rainfall of 3.20 inches fell near Sloat through the morning of the 2nd.

Water washed over highway 1 between Cedarville and Fort Bidwell in multiple areas. In some areas, the water was over 20 feet wide.  A spotter just northeast of Fort Bidwell reported 1 inch of rain between 0100PST and 0700PST, with 1.5 to 1.8 inches in 24 hours in Cedarville and Fort Bidwell.

The California Highway Patrol reported boulders on highway 89 near Emerald Bay State Park. An estimated 2 to 3 inches of precipitation was reported (SNOTEL/RAWS observations), mostly within the previous 12 hours.

Valley wind gusts between 60 and 70 mph were noted from the morning of the 1st into the morning of the 2nd, with the most widespread coverage early on the 2nd. In the foothills, wind gusts were between 70 and 88 mph. At Virginia Peak, winds gusted to 140 mph. Damage reports included downed fences and power lines in southwest Reno and in the Minden-Gardnerville area, several trucks overturned in Washoe Valley, and damage to a transmitter at KOLO (Reno) which knocked a broadcast off the air. Finally, high winds caused the cancellation of a number of flights at the Reno-Tahoe airport during the afternoon and evening of 12/1.

Winds gusted between 60 and 80 mph in and near Hawthorne on the 2nd, with up to 60 mph in the Mason Valley and up to 72 mph at the Brawley Peak RAWS. Winds caused power outages and roof damage in Yerington with damage to a facade and a street sign blown down in Hawthorne.

Winds gusted between 60 and 69 mph west of Fallon and Lovelock on the 2nd, including Stagecoach, Silver Springs, and Pyramid Lake. The largest impact was noted in Nixon, where a spotter noted shingles off rooves, a trailer overturned, a greenhouse and fences blown down, and tree branches broken.

Two to four inches of snow fell between Hawthorne and Luning with little or no snow north and west of Hawthorne. However, from Luning to Mina (and likely across much of eastern Mineral County), 4 to 7 inches of snow fell from the evening of the 12th through mid morning on the 13th. The snow caused school transportation in Mineral County to be suspended on the 13th.

Winds gusted between 60 and 77 mph during the afternoon of the 21st, with the highest winds in the foothills west of highway 395. These winds caused several tractor trailer trucks to be blown over on highway 395 between the Stead and Red Rock exits (North Valleys of Reno). In addition, at least 3 planes were diverted from the Reno-Tahoe airport with sustained winds over 40 mph between 1200PST and 1300PST.

Avalanche control activities (explosives) at the Alpine Meadows Ski resort resulted in the death of an experienced ski patroller. The avalanche broke much wider and higher than expected based on past experience. The man was found and uncovered within 8 minutes of the avalanche. He was airlifted via CareFlight helicopter to Renown Medical Center in Reno where he died.

One and a half to 2.5 feet of snow fell south of highway 50 with 2.5 to 4 feet (locally 4 to 5 feet) north of highway 50 between the afternoon of the 21st and late evening on the 23rd. In addition to heavy snow, winds gusted peridiodically to between 30 and 40 mph bringing restricted visibility at times.

A large range of snowfall was reported on the 22nd and 23rd. For the lower valleys along the highway 395 corridor, 1 to 3 inches of snowfall was common. However, in the foothills 6 to 12 inches with local amounts as high as 15 to 19 inches were noted. Some notable totals include 7.5 inches in Cold Springs, 15 inches 2 miles west of Verdi, and 16 inches 5 miles southwest of New Washoe City.

A solid 1 to 2 feet of snow fell near and west of highway 395 north of Janesville with 3 or more feet in the Feather River Basin along highways 70 and 89 from Portola north and west.  At the Grizzly Ridge HADS (12 miles WNW Portola at 6900 feet), 7.5 inches of liquid equivalent precipitation fell which likely translates to at least 5 to 7 feet of snow.

A widespread two to three feet of snow fell from midday on the 21th through late evening on the 23rd in the Lake Tahoe area, with 4 to 5 feet near the crest and at higher elevations. In addition to heavy snow, winds gusted between 35 and 45 mph at times for periods of significantly reduced visibility.

Two to 4 feet of snow, highest at the immediate Sierra crest, fell west of highway 395 from the evening of the 21st through early morning on the 24th. Near and east of highway 395, 1 to 2 feet of snow fell as far south as Mammoth Lakes (only 9 inches at Crowley Lake). In addition to heavy snow, winds gusted to between 35 and 50 mph at times along highway 395.
A widespread 8 to 13 inches of snow fell in the Lake Tahoe Basin east of highway 89 with this system. For areas along and west of highway 89, 15 to 20 inches of snow fell.
A widespread 12 to 18 inches of snow fell with this system.

A widespread 1 to 3 inches of snow fell with this system. However, some areas in the foothills and between Washoe Valley and Carson City received 4 to 7 inches of snow. Some of the heavier snow totals may have been enhanced by lake effect snow off of Lake Tahoe, especially in the early morning hours of the 26th.

Along and east of highway 395, 4 to 8 inches (locally to 9 inches) of snow fell with this system. For areas west of highway 395, one to 2 feet of snow fell with local amounts up to 29 inches near Mammoth Mountain.
One to three inches of snow (locally to 4 inches in Lovelock) fell from the afternoon of the 25th through early morning on the 26th, mainly north of highway 50 as evidenced by  the KRGX radar.

Winds gusted between 40 and 52 mph across much of the area from the afternoon of the 9th through early morning on the 10th. However, Walker Lake RAWS experienced much stronger winds with winds sustained between 38 and 50 mph with gusts between 60 and 73 mph between 0200PST and 0400PST on the 10th.

Several days with lows in the single digits to as low as -14F (South Lake Tahoe airport) and highs in the upper 20s to mid 30s caused pipes to burst at 4 casinos in Stateline on the 13th and 14th. The burst pipes caused water damage to the 18th floor at Harrah's and flooding of casino floors and stores at Harvey's Casino.

Four to 6 inches of snow fell from near Lake City north to Fort Bidwell from the evening of the 18th through early morning on the 19th. Cedarville only received 3 inches as reported by a CO-OP observer.

Widespread wind gusts of 58 to 66 mph occurred along and west of highway 395 and Interstate 580 from Washoe Valley south in addition to the southwest and northern portions of Reno. In the foothills west of Reno and Carson City, winds gusted between 75 and 81 mph with brief gusts as high as 92 mph on the south end of Washoe Valley around 1430PST. High winds caused power outages in Caughlin Ranch (SW Reno) and Carson City, with power poles knocked down in Carson City. Around 6700 customers were affected by power outages on the afternoon of the 20th.
Heavy rain with slow-moving thunderstorms over the Lake Range east of Pyramid Lake caused up to a dozen sections of highway 447 between Nixon and Gerlach to be washed out.
Slow-moving thunderstorms with heavy rainfall caused flash flooding over highway 447 about 5 miles northwest of Gerlach. The road was closed due to the flooding.
The wind gusts were recorded at the Stagecoach NDOT sensor.
This wind gust was recorded at the Juniper Springs RAWS.

Hail between 0.75 and 1.5 inches in diameter was reported by several spotters in the North Valleys of Reno. The largest hail report was near the Stead airport which had between 1.25 and 1.50 inch diameter hail. Cold Springs (northwest part of hail track) only had hail to 0.75 inches in diameter. Picture evidence of the hail size was sent to the National Weather Service.

Five lightning strikes associated with a severe thunderstorm hit the Washoe County Emergency Operations Center's communications tower. The strikes disabled the primary communications repeater although backups were not disabled.
A Facebook video from the public showed rapidly flowing water over Milan Drive in an industrial area. The water overflowed the drainage ditch alongside the road.
Nickel sized hail and heavy rain fell near Eagle Lake.
Wind gust measured at the Ash Valley RAWS.

Thunderstorms with torrential rains produced flooding of roads in the north Spanish Springs area with flowing water crossing several residential streets. No significant damage or rescues were noted though. Copious small hail mixed in with the flood waters producing hail drifts of 1-2 feet deep in some yards. Mesonet station nearby (DW4148 Sparks) measured 1.87 inches of rain, with 0.96 inches falling in 16 minutes.

The Lovelock ASOS reported visibility as low as 1/4 mile with between 1/4 and 1/2 mile between about 1730PST and 1815PST. The low visibilities likely affected Interstate 80. Thunderstorms caused widespread wind gusts between 40-50 mph in Pershing, Churchill and northern Lyon Counties.
Wind gusts 59 to 66 mph were reported at the Walker Lake NDOT sensor.
Wind gust measured at NWS Reno.

Thunderstorm outflows of 50-60 mph caused blowing dust which reduced visibilities down to 1/8 mile in Fernley and Fallon with 3/4 mile at the Lovelock airport. The 60 mph gust was recorded at the Fallon Naval Air Station. A Facebook photo near Lovelock clearly showed a wall of dust (haboob).
Nickel sized hail was reported 4 miles west of Portola.
Nickel sized hail reported just east of Sloat.

Heavy rain on steep terrain caused a debris flow which covered around a 300 foot portion of Interstate 80 on the westbound side with up to 8 inches of mud and debris. The interstate was closed for about 30 minutes on the eastbound side and several hours on the westbound side. At least 6 weeks of rehabilitation to prevent further debris flows was required on the shoulder and steep terrain near the freeway.
Reports from the Mono County sheriff and the California Highway Patrol indicated hail between 0.75 and 1 inch in diameter. Hail covered highway 182 in Bridgeport to 4 inches in depth.

Eight homes along highway 182 in Bridgeport received water damage including one home with a flooded basement and another with several inches of water on the main floor. Time estimated based on period of heavy rain in radar.
Hail between 0.88 and 1 inch.

Training thunderstorms brought very heavy rain to the Fernley area during the afternoon and evening of the 4th. Flash flooding caused a 10 ft sinkhole to form near the intersection of Cable Canyon Rd and Seabiscuit Dr.
Three feet of standing water was reported on Scott Drive in Fernley.
Interstate 80 was closed between exits 43 and 46 between about 1600PST and 1730PST due to very heavy rain on the freeway causing a large amount of ponding water.

The Lyon County sheriff reported house and yard flooding near Saddlehorn Way, Mallard Way and Jenny's Lane. In addition, the Wendy's in central Fernley noted flooding. Three waves of heavy thunderstorm rainfall produced up to 1.3 inches of rain (per spotter reports) between about 1500PST and 1900PST.
Measured at the Majuba mesonet site.

Wind gusts between 60 and 77 mph were recorded at the NWS Reno office. The source of the wind gusts was not clear as it could have been from a nearby shower or a larger scale outflow from thunderstorms in the Sierra.
Measured at the NWS Reno office.
A thunderstorm dropped some hail to the size of nickels mixed in with mainly pea-sized hail.

Six to 8 inches of mud and debris covered the westbound lanes of Interstate 80. The westbound lanes of the interstate between the Nevada state line and the Farad exit were closed until 2100PST. One lane of eastbound I-80 was also closed (to allow westbound traffic to turn around).
Flash flooding and a road wash out on highway 338 was reported by Nevada DOT. Several days of thunderstorms with heavy rainfall noted on highway 338 near Sweetwater Summit.
Penny to nickel hail was reported in South Lake Tahoe with hail accumulations up to 2 inches deep.
A 3-inch diameter apple tree and 30 feet of fence was blown over due to thunderstorm outflow.
Measured at Juniper Springs RAWS station.
Measured at Walker Lake RAWS. Time of gust between 1739PST and 1759PST.

Spotters in the Antelope Valley near Coleville indicated periodic low visibility due to smoke from the Rim Fire. In addition, visibilities from the Mountain Warfare Training Center (KBAN) indicated visibilities down to 1/2 mile as times.

Dense smoke and the associated poor air quality from the Rim Fire continued to periodically affect Alpine County through the end of the month although areas north near South Lake Tahoe generally saw some improvement after the 28th. Medical facilities in the South Lake Tahoe area noted around 5 to 10 visits per day related to respiratory problems (versus 1 or 2 a day normally in late summer) through the 28th.

Dense smoke from the Rim Fire near Yosemite brought periodic low visibilities and poor air quality to areas from Alpine County north to South Lake Tahoe. Visibilities down to 1/4 mile were reported near Markleeville with visibility down to 1/2 mile at the South Lake Tahoe airport. The low visibility caused the cancellation of an air show at the airport.

The California Highway Patrol reported 3 to 4 inches of water over highway 120 in Benton Hot Springs with 4 to 6 inches of water in a residence. The road was washed out with mud and debris in roadway.

Lyon County officials reported a debris flow (mainly mud/small rocks) which covered Artesia Road to a depth of 3 feet and a width of 200 to 300 feet during the evening of the 14th. The flow was caused by heavy thunderstorm rain on the Bison Fire scar.
Tree branches 4 to 6 inches in diameter were blown onto mobile home roof. The roof of the mobile home was penetrated.

The Nevada Highway Patrol reported up to 3 dozen accidents in the Reno area on icy roads caused by freezing rain late on the 20th and early on the 21st. The majority of accidents were on Interstate 580 between Interstate 80 and the Mt Rose exit. Up to 15 vehicles were involved in one incident which closed Interstate 580 for two hours.
A widespread 4 to 8 inches of snow fell near and north of highway 50 on the 3rd. Some totals south of Reno were likely enhanced by lake effect snow off of Lake Tahoe.
Six to 8 inches of snow fell in Plumas and Sierra Counties, generally near and south of highway 70.

Four to 7 inches of snow fell across northern Pershing County as a cold front moved through the region. Snowfall is estimated based on snow water equivalent from Rye Patch Reservoir and measured snowfall at the Winnemucca airport (Humboldt County).

A cold front moved through western Nevada early on the 7th bringing 4 to 6 inches of snow on the north and west side of Reno and in the Minden-Gardnerville area. For the Carson City area, 6 to 10 inches of snowfall was reported. The snowfall near Carson City was likely enhanced by lake effect snow bands off of Lake Tahoe.
A cold front moved through early on the 7th bringing 13 to 17 inches of snowfall to the Carson Range.
A widespread 10 to 20 inches of snow fell along and ahead of a cold front which moved through the region early on the 7th.
The California Highway Patrol indicated dense fog along highway 395 between Doyle and Susanville. The fog contributed to several accidents on highway 395.

Snow levels were initially high (around 7500-8000 feet) as the storm began on the afternoon of the 29th. However, as the storm progressed southeast overnight into the 30th, snow levels fell below 5500 feet bringing heavy snow to areas south and east of Lake Tahoe. Snowfall totals south of Lake Tahoe were between 10 and 17 inches on the 30th.
Snowfall totals ranged from 10 to 14 inches along highway 395 from Lee Vining north. Near the Sierra crest, SNOTEL and Mammoth ski area sites indicated between 12 and 18 inches of snowfall.

Between 12 and 18 inches of snow fell in the Carson Range from near Incline Village (Diamond Peak ski area) south to Marlette Lake on the 20th. At Lake Tahoe level, the Glenbrook CO-OP site reported 9 inches of snowfall.

Five to 10 inches of snow fell between Carson City and Minden-Gardnerville on the 30th, with 12 inches of snow in Double Springs (5 miles north of Topaz Lake). Power was knocked out per a report 3 miles NNE of Topaz Lake.
Two to three feet (locally to 3.5 feet) of heavy, wet snow fell above 7,000-7,500 feet on the 8th and 9th. Below 7,000 feet, precipitation fell mostly as rain.

The Mount Rose and Diamond Peak ski areas reported between 2 and 3 feet of heavy, wet snow on the 8th and 9th. South of highway 50, 14 inches was reported at the Daggett Pass Fire Station. Below 7,000 feet, 10 inches of snow fell in Incline Village down to 6,700 feet. Near Lake Tahoe level, precipitation fell mostly as rain.

Most areas in the Reno-Carson City-Minden area recorded wind gusts of between 40 and 50 mph on the 8th. However, foothill areas along Interstate 580 south of Reno (very wind prone) reported wind gusts of 60 to 73 mph. The strong winds caused trees to be downed along with the spilling of large boulders onto a I-580 access road at the south end of Washoe Valley.
The Surprise Valley RAWS reported wind gusts as high as 71 mph on the 12th. Meanwhile, a home weather station in Fort Bidwell recorded wind gusts up to 63 mph.
Wind gust up to 73 mph were noted at the Surprise Valley RAWS on the 15th. Meanwhile, a home weather station in Fort Bidwell recorded wind gusts up to 69 mph.

High winds were reported along highway 395 south of Susanville on the 15th. Wind gusts up to 71 mph were noted at the Doyle RAWS with gusts up to 60 mph in Janesville. Five miles northwest of Susanville, power lines were reported down by a spotter.

Gusts between 60 and 76 mph were indicated by RAWS stations between Coleville and Bridgeport as well as the Mammoth AWOS. Highway 395 was closed between Lee Vining and Bridgeport with two tractor trailer trucks blown over.

Widespread wind gusts between 60 and 70 mph were noted on the north, west, and southwest sides of Reno as well as in portions of the Carson Valley. In the foothills along Interstate 580, wind gusts of 80 to 90 mph were recorded. The high winds brought a few fences down in Golden Valley and in Spanish Springs. In southwest Reno, small trees were uprooted along with some power outages.

Two outbuildings were destroyed and around 15 trees were uprooted as a cold front moved through Hidden Valley. Also, a 2 X 4 from one of the outbuildings was driven into the side of a home. A wind gust to 52 mph was recorded at the UNR Ag Farm about a half-mile northeast of the damage site. However, based on wind studies for the enhanced Fujita scale regarding the uprooting of coniferous trees a much higher speed was estimated at the damage site.

Most areas in the Reno-Carson City area noted wind gusts between 40 and 50 mph early on the 6th. However, wind prone areas recorded wind gusts of 60 to 65 mph. Winds caused a 10 X 20 metal shed to come apart on the north side of Carson City and cause damage to a vehicle. An NDOT observation about 1/4 mile northwest of the damage recorded a wind gust to 63 mph at 545PST.

Most of the Tahoe Basin received between 3 and 8 inches of snow on the 29th due to a mix of rain and snow below 7000 feet. However, the higher elevations near the crest received between 1 and 2 feet of snow including 12 inches at Northstar Ski and 20 inches at the Squaw Valley Ski area.

Most areas of Mono County received only a very light snowfall on the 31st. However, areas west of highway 395 near Mammoth Lakes received considerably more including 12 inches at the Mammoth Lakes Ranger Station and 20 inches at the Mammoth Ski area.

A wide range of snowfall fell with this system on the 25th. Areas below 6500 feet east of highway 89 in the Tahoe Basin generally received only up to 3 inches of snowfall. Meanwhile, areas west of highway 89 below 7000 feet saw 5-9 inches of snow, with areas near the crest receiving upwards of 18 inches.

This event was mainly restricted to the high Sierra west of highway 395 where up to around 2 feet of snow fell near Mammoth Mountain. Areas near and east of highway 395 received much less with only up to 3 inches observed.

Most areas saw wind gusts to between 40 and 50 mph early on the 22nd. However, the Galena RAWS and Reno-Tahoe airport noted wind gusts between 60 and 66 mph, along with sustained winds over 40 mph for the airport from 0018PST to 0143PST. While wind speeds decreased later in the morning, erratic wind shifts near the front (around 0730PST) at the Reno airport led to low level wind shear and major concerns for the airport (although no incidents were noted). Finally, a large part of a tree was broken in Sparks early in the morning.

A significant amount of water over state road 121 was reported by NDOT. There was  also rock and dirt debris with the fast-flowing water which caused the closure of the road. The time of the flash flood was estimated based on radar as the reports were received after the actual event.

Widespread visibility less than 1/4 mile were reported in the Reno area and east to around Fernley. The dust was carried by large-scale thunderstorm outflows bringing east to northeast winds of 15-25 mph with gusts to 40-50 mph.

An image from highway 447 between Fernley and Nixon and a report of visibility less than 1/4 mile in Fernley confirmed a dust storm west of Lovelock and Fallon. The dust was carried by large-scale thunderstorm outflows which brought east to northeast winds of 15-25 mph with gusts to 40 mph.
Wind gust measured at Little Valley RAWS. Gust between 1438 and 1538PST...exact time of gust estimated from radar.
Wind gust at the Five Mile Flat NDOT sensor. The gust was caused by an outflow from earlier thunderstorms to the south of the sensor.
Outflow from earlier thunderstorms to the south of the Reno-Tahoe International airport brought this gust.
Multiple reports of large tree limbs downed along Sparks Blvd. and at the Sparks Marina.
Wind gust at NWS Reno office. Gust caused by large outflow from earlier thunderstorms well south of office.
Wind gust at Doyle RAWS. Wind gust between 1711 and 1811PST...exact time estimated from radar.
Hail reported by Mono County Sheriff's department.
Measured at the NWS office in Reno.

A spotter reported that highway 359 south of Hawthorne and Lucky Boy Pass Road were closed due to flash flooding/debris flows. At least one vehicle was stranded in mud. A video was shared on Facebook showing fast-flowing water over highway 359.

The California Highway Patrol (CHP) reported water covering Lundy Lake Road, with the Mono County Sheriff noting a large and deep mudslide over the road. CHP indicated that emergency crews were unable to reach an emergency call due to the road blockage.
Hail report near Carson City High School.
Measured at the NWS Reno office.
Maximum wind gust measured at the Dead Camel RAWS between 1347PST and 1447PST. Time of gust estimated from radar.
Wind gust measured at the Bull Flat RAWS.

A line of thunderstorms initiated an extensive gust front, which moved north bringing winds 25 to 40 mph with gusts to around 60 mph. The Pershing County Sheriff's office (as well as photographic evidence) indicated a large dust storm with near zero visibility along highway 95 north of Fallon and on Interstate 80 between Fernley and Winnemucca.
The Silver Springs airport measured sustained winds of 40 mph with a gust to 60 mph.
The Lovelock airport measured sustained winds of 44 mph with gusts to 61 mph.
Pictures and videos corroborated a rapid increase in water levels which threatened building damage and caused some vehicles to stall near Meadowood Mall.

Water over roads and mud debris along and near Center Drive were reported (including pictures and videos) by a fire department official. Extensive damage to streets due to undermining was noted along with minor water and mud intrusions into several homes. One home had up to a foot of water and mud in the garage along with damage to the garage door. The time of the event is estimated.
A Facebook photo and a report from Douglas County Emergency Management indicated a large mud flow across Long Dr. The time of the event is estimated but was likely between 1330PST and 1430PST.
Homeowner called 911 to report water flowing into his home at 1319PST. At least 5 other homes indicated mud (up to 3 to 5 feet) and water flows, with a video showing fast-flowing water down a street.

A spotter reported debris and rocks in roadways near Windmill and Fish Springs Road around 1400PST. A short time later the spotter noted that Windmill Road was washed out and Calle Del Sol was impassable. The spotter's rain gauge recorded 1.10 of rain between 1300PST and 1325PST.
Half-dollar sized hail was reported in the Palomino Valley.
Estimated nickel-sized hail.

A spotter reported that Pine Nut Creek was flooding near Lena Lane. The Minden-Gardnerville Record Courier received a report from the owner of City of Refuge (just downstream from Lena Ln) indicating flooding of the property's orchards. One home was flooded on Blue Sage Rd.

The Minden-Gardnerville Record Courier noted that a Douglas County fire marshal stated that 9 houses had interior damage due to flooding. Also, emergency officials indicated that 2 feet of water had flowed over Fish Springs Rd. A power pole was broken near Jacobsen Ln due to the flash flood.

Flood waters from Pine Nut Creek moved over East Valley Rd (and several non-paved roads) per photographic evidence.  The Allerman Canal (eastern side of Gardnerville) helped to stop the advance of flood waters. The time of the flash flood is estimated.
This wind gust was measured at a Citizen Weather Observer Program (CWOP) site.
The hail was measured by a ranger at Washoe Lake State Park and relayed by a spotter.
Small tree branches were reported down near New Washoe City.
The hail occurred at McQueen High School.
Dime to nickel-sized hail was reported in Gerlach.
Wind gusts between 60 and 65 mph were recorded at the Cherry Valley RAWS. The time of the wind gusts were estimated based on radar.
Up to 2 feet of mud was reported across state highway 121 (Dixie Valley Rd) around 10 miles north of the intersection with highway 50.

High winds were recorded in the foothills around Reno, at the Reno airport and in portions of the north valleys of Reno on the 14th and 15th. The Galena RAWS and Five Mile Flat NDOT sensors had the highest wind gusts (81 and 77 mph, respectively), with gusts up to 68 mph at the Stead airport and 61 mph at the Reno-Tahoe International Airport. Sporadic power outages were noted on the 14th and 15th.

High wind gusts were recorded at various sites late in the evening of the 28th into the early morning hours of the 29th. The highest wind gust (81 mph) was recorded at the Galena RAWS, with many other sites noting wind gusts between 60 and 70 mph. Winds caused a tree near downtown Reno to snap near its base and cause minor damage to a home.

The Glenbrook and Dagget Pass Fire Stations responded to numerous incidents of fallen trees and downed power lines due to high winds between Cave Rock and Kingsbury Grade. One tree fell onto a house resulting in major damage, with at least 7 homes damaged in all. A small fire was noted due to a downed power line north of Cave Rock.|Winds gusted between 45-70 mph below 7,500 feet, with a gust to 112 mph atop Slide Mountain. Damages from this event are a rough estimate.

Widespread wind gusts over 65 mph were noted on the 11th, with the highest gusts (over 80 mph) west of highway 395 in the foothills and the southwestern Carson Valley. There were an exceptionally high number of damage reports including power lines and trees downed (knocking out power to more than 10,000), fences damaged, and a semi-truck blown over on Interstate 80. In addition, winds caused more than 30 flight cancellations at the Reno-Tahoe International airport.  Damages from this event are a rough estimate.

Winds gusted to 60 and 70 mph at the Truckee and South Lake Tahoe airports, respectively, on the morning of the 11th. Over the Sierra ridges, winds gusted as high as 135 mph. Numerous trees and power lines were downed, along with damage to several homes and vehicles due to fallen trees. The power outages, some lasting up to 2 days, caused South Lake Tahoe schools to be closed through the 12th. Finally, winds downed a tree which caused the death of a teenager in a heavily wooded area. Damages from this event are a rough estimate.

Downslope winds gusted to between 65 and 80 mph near the highway 395 corridor. Locally higher winds to over 100 mph occurred near the highway 395 and state route 167 junction (near Mono City) shortly after 1100PST, with reports of windows shattered and roof shingles blown off. Also, a roof blew off a home and serious damage was noted at a gas station awning in Lee Vining.

A widespread 1 to 2 inches of snow fell in the Reno and Carson City-Minden areas during the early morning of the 30th. However, a band of heavier snow with 3 to 5 inches was reported in south and southwest Reno as well as in Virginia City and Carson City. Locally higher amounts of more than 6 inches were noted in the Palomino Valley near Pyramid Lake, likely caused by lake effect enhancement.
A spotter one mile west of Doyle received 12 inches of snow. The snowfall was likely enhanced by lake effect snow off of Pyramid Lake.
Up to a foot of water over low spots in Johnson Lane. Water reported in two homes.
Wind gusts of 61 to 70 mph were recorded at the Surprise Valley RAWS.

Wind gusts of 60 to 79 mph were recorded on the 6th, with 79 mph measured at the Doyle RAWS near highway 395. The high winds caused 2 semi trucks to overturn on highway 395 between Susanville and Janesville, with visibility in that area dropping to less than 1/2 mile at times due to blowing dust. Also, a 2 foot diameter tree in Graeagle fell over and split an outbuilding in two. Finally, an aerial survey by the U.S. Forest Service estimated that over 71K trees were broken or blown over, mostly in western Lassen County but with some of that number in adjacent counties to the west and southwest. Wind directions were atypical (south to southeast) for the magnitude of the winds and this likely boosted the number of downed trees.

Wind gusts largely between 50 and 60 mph were noted on the 6th, with winds in South Lake Tahoe gusting as high as 64 mph. The winds caused more than a dozen 1 to 3 foot diameter trees to be blown over or uprooted, with one tree falling on a home. The fallen trees also knocked down power lines in and near South Lake Tahoe.

Widespread wind gusts between 63 and 82 mph were noted near highway 395. However, the Bridgeport RAWS measured a wind gust to 91 mph. Numerous trees (up to 18 in diameter) were downed near Mono City, with some broken windows and roof damage noted as well. According to the Mammoth Times, power lines were downed which caused widespread power outages north of Mammoth for at least a day.

Wind gusts of 58 and 64 mph were measured at the Bulls Eye and Little Valley RAWS, respectively. However, strong downslope winds on the lower slopes of the Carson Range brought wind gusts over 80 mph, with a gusts to 109 mph between 1350PST and 1450PST at the Galena RAWS.

Widespread wind gusts of 60 to 79 mph were recorded from Minden north to the Palomino Valley (southwest of Pyramid Lake). Higher gusts of 80 to 90 mph were noted in the Virginia Range and southwest of Gardnerville, with gusts over 100 mph at the Galena RAWS. Numerous roof and fences were damaged and several 4 foot diameter trees were downed on power lines in Gardnerville. Longtime residents of the area said this was the worst windstorm they had experienced in over 10 years. As many as 21,000 were without power around the area, with the worst damage to power lines in Douglas County. Finally, the high winds were blamed for the loss of power to 2 emergency communications repeaters (Eagle Ridge and Como) critical to Lyon County.

Wind gusts to 63 mph were measured in the Smith and Mason Valleys, with a gust to 86  mph near Sweetwater Summit. Alternate highway 95 east of Yerington was closed for a few hours due to several accidents, with high winds and very low visibility due to blowing dust reported by the Lyon County EM.

Extreme downslope winds in the lee of the Sierra prompted rapid spread of the Round Fire, which raced up a drainage and burned 40 homes in Swall Meadows.  The size of the fire was 6,537 acres according to CalOES. Precipitation arrived early in the morning on the 7th which dramatically slowed the fire, although the fire was not completely contained until the 12th.
The Mount Rose Ski area (above 8500 ft) reported 19 to 24 inches of heavy, wet snow.

Between 1 and 2 feet of snow fell on the east side of Lake Tahoe and in the Carson Range, including 13 inches in Glenbrook, 16 inches at the Mount Rose Ski area and 24 inches for the Diamond Peak ski area.

Ski areas and an avalanche forecaster (Sierra Avalanche Center) around the Lake Tahoe area reported 14 to 28 inches of snowfall, with the highest amounts near the crest. At lake level snow amounts varied greatly, with a spotter near Meyers indicating 13 inches but many other areas around the lake and near Truckee only reporting between 5 and 9 inches.

A widespread snowfall of between 0.5 and 3 inches was noted around the Reno and Carson City area. However, higher amounts fell in the foothills west of Carson City (up to 8 inches) and from the north valleys of Reno (3 to 6 inches) north to the Palomino Valley and the Red Rock area (8 to 15 inches).
The Nevada Division of Emergency Management reported golf-ball sized hail.

The storm survey was supplemented by a public video of the tornado moving along 5th street in Hawthorne. The tornado was determined to be EF-1 for 0.3 miles on the east side of Hawthorne (near 5th street) and EF-0 elsewhere. Approximately 10 to 15 homes and businesses were severely damaged along with power lines and road signs. One 2 foot diameter tree was blown over onto a mobile home and 2 vehicles were severely damaged. This tornado was associated with a non-supercell thunderstorm.

Snow from the afternoon of the 7th through the morning of the 8th caused the closure of the Sierra crest passes and chain controls for most of highway 395. Snowfall amounts were generally between 7 and 12 inches above 7,000 feet, with 4 to 8 inches down to around 6,000 feet. Locally higher amounts to 14 inches were noted in Lee Vining, with possible higher amounts to between 14 and 19 inches at the Sierra crest per SNOTEL observations.
Peak wind measured between 1245 and 1345PST, with the time of the gust estimated from radar.
Three separate Facebook posts and a Twitter post showed pictorial evidence a non-supercell tornado (landspout most likely) east of highway 395 in Lassen County.

Per a spotter report, 1.13 inches of rain fell in about an hour in the Six Mile Canyon area near the Lyon and Storey County line. Lyon County Emergency Management  received reports of significant yard and landscaping damage as well as water in garages. Also, heavy equipment was required to remove mud from streets in the Mark Twain community as well as in Six Mile Canyon (Storey County).
The Douglas County Emergency Manager reported flash flooding impacts near low water crossings along Sawmill and Arroyo Roads.

The Douglas County Emergency Manager reported 9 homes with damage due to flooding near the low water crossings in the Ruhenstroth subdivision area. A fire chief noted that the completely dry Pine Nut Creek was rapidly filled with a 4 to 5 foot wall of water.
A small, high based (likely above 12,000 ft AGL) thunderstorm produced the severe gust. The gust was recorded at a Nevada DOT site.
Wind gusts between 59 and 74 mph were recorded at the Bull Flat RAWS between 1740PST and 1940PST. Time of severe gusts are approximate and based on radar signatures.

Slow-moving thunderstorms with torrential rainfall in the higher terrain overwhelmed city drainage systems, causing flash flooding in East Sparks. Some areas were under several feet of water, with standing water and debris making travel difficult along Sparks and Vista Blvds. According to Sparks Police at least a dozen cars were stuck in the flooding. Water damage to Whitehead and Moss Elementary Schools was estimated at between 400K and 450K.
Measured at the NWS office.
A mudslide over highway 89 just east of Markleeville caused the road to become impassable.

Lyon County Emergency Management reported that highway 342 through Silver City was flooded with water, gravel and debris. Traffic was diverted to an alternate truck route. The time of the flooding is estimated based on radar.
Facebook videos from a National Weather Service employee and KOLO News showed fast flowing water in Pine Nut Creek and over low water crossings on Cali Pequeno and Out-R-Way Roads.
The Nevada DOT reported a flash flood and rock slide along state route 360. The time of the flash flood is approximate and based on radar.

CALTRANS reported a debris flow in the area of Wolf Creek Road and highway 4, which is in the Washington Fire burn scar area. A debris flow also occurred on highway 89 south of Markleeville. A National Weather Service employee noted about 3 feet of dirt piled up on the sides of the road the day after the flow.
A rock and mud slide was reported on highway 120 by the California Highway Patrol.
A spotter in the Six Mile Canyon/Samuel Clemens area reported 1.15 of rainfall in less than 30 minutes. Water was flowing into homes with property damage.

The Lyon County Sheriff's office reported a car stuck in water flowing over V and T Way from a dry wash. The car had to be pulled out by heavy machinery. Pictures of the incident indicate that the water was approximately 18 inches deep at the time of the rescue.

The Douglas County Sheriff's Office reported that various places along Foothill Blvd.  experienced flash flooding, which made roads impassable. A spotter in the flash flood area noted 1.65 of rainfall in 45 minutes.

Thunderstorm outflow produced this peak wind gust at the Reno-Tahoe International Airport. The Reno ATC Tower indicated that a Cessna aircraft was flipped by the strong winds (no damage estimate given).
This was a peak wind gust measured at the National Weather Service.
The hail was measured at the Long Valley Agricultural Inspection Station.
KRNV News 4 posted a picture of a 70 foot tree which fell onto a house in Sparks.
The hail was estimated to be golf-ball sized from a Facebook image. The hail broke flower pots, a birdbath and two glass tables.
Hail size was estimated by spotter.

Two photographs indicated a waterspout on Lake Tahoe. Eyewitnesses noted that the waterspout started near the mouth of Emerald Bay and moved quickly southeast towards Tahoe Keys. The waterspout dissipated before reaching land.

Very heavy rainfall caused water to overflow washes and overwhelm drainage infrastructure in the Johnson Lane area. Water damage to 141 properties, including major damage to 4 homes and minor damage to 7 homes, was reported by Douglas County Emergency Management officials. Damages are estimated and may include some costs from flooding on July 9 (total damage 2.2M between the two days).
Photographic evidence shows a vehicle stuck in flood waters on Prospect St. The occupant abandoned the vehicle and was rescued by fire department officials.
Wind gusts of 61 to 63 mph were recorded at the Naval Air Station in Fallon. The highest wind gust was recorded at at 1505PST.

Multiple videos from Reno news media (on Facebook) showed fast-flowing water over Stephanie Way and over low-water crossings at East Valley Road and Nye Dr. (near Johnson Lane). Douglas County sheriff's deputies noted several road closures in the area. Around 21 properties experienced damage from the flash flooding. Damages are approximate and based on the dividing of Douglas County Emergency Management's damage estimates for both July 8 and 9.

Reports from the Nevada Department of Transportation indicated water and debris over highway 447 south of Empire. The flooding caused significant erosion of road shoulders which required closure of the road for safety and repairs.

A CALTRANS official reported up to 4 feet of mud and debris over highway 395 near the burn scar from the Red Rock Fire (fire occurred in 2013). It took 5 hours to clear all the debris off of the road, with one car getting stuck in the debris (necessitating a rescue).
This wind gust was measured at the Juniper Springs RAWS.
This wind gust was measured at the Bull Flat RAWS.
Accumulating nickel-sized hail was reported near the Lake Davis Dam.

Numerous pictures showed the aftermath of a flash flood in the canyon/alluvial fan west of the small community of Marietta. Minor damage was noted to area roads (unpaved) and a wire mesh fence. The time of the flood was estimated from radar.
Wind gust reported at the Dead Camel RAWS due to nearby very high-based showers. The time of the gust was between 0547PST and 0647PST, with exact time estimated by radar.

Heavy rain upstream in the White Mountains caused flash flooding, both on highway 6 with mud and debris over the road (causing a closure), and in the town of Chalfant with 20 homes damaged from flood waters. Four or 5 of those homes (on Sacramento St) suffered major damage per a Cal OES report. The timing of the flash flood is estimated from between the time highway 6 was reported to have debris over it until about one hour after flooding reached the town of Chalfant (times on CHP incident page).

One to 4 inches of snow was reported between the 2nd and 3rd above the lower valley floors. A medical condition (primary cause per investigators) combined with the snow and cold to cause severe hypothermia in an elderly man. He went out for a walk the afternoon of the 2nd and was not found until late morning on the 3rd. He was alive but later died at the hospital. The victim was found at around 6,200 feet in the Brunswick Canyon area.

Twelve to 18 inches of snow fell near the Sierra crest and in the Sweetwater Range of northern Mono County above 8,500 to 9,000 feet. Lesser amounts of 5 to 11 inches fell down to 7,500 feet, with up to an inch down to 6,500 feet.

Widespread snow totals of 5 to 10 inches were noted in the Reno-Sparks area, highest on the north and west side of Reno (in lake effect band from Lake Tahoe). From the north valleys of Reno to Palomino Valley and Red Rock Rd near the California border lake effect snow from Pyramid Lake boosted snowfall totals to 8 to 15 inches, with the highest amounts in the Antelope and Hungry Valleys. Numerous broken tree branches were noted due to the heavy, wet snow and over 35,000 customers were without power in Washoe County due to downed power lines (morning of 11/10).

Four to 6 inches of heavy, wet snow (6-7 to 1 snow to liquid ratio) fell on the 24th south and west of Susanville, including the Sierra Valley and near Bieber. Eleven inches was reported just southeast of Lake Davis at 6000 feet.

Heavy snowfall of 8 to 15 inches fell from the Truckee airport to along and west of highway 89 on the 24th, with the highest amount in the Tahoe-Donner area. Lesser amounts of 5 to 7 inches fell for most other locations. Areas from Homewood to Glenshire reported 4 inches of snowfall between 1000PST and 1400PST.

Winds gusted to between 58 and 68 mph with some sustained winds over 40 mph from Reno south to Washoe Valley. Winds caused a semi to be blown over on southbound McCarran Blvd in Sparks, with the road closed for a time between Prater and Victorian. Also, a power pole was knocked down in Sparks. In Reno/Stead, a fence was blown down into a window with one of the fence's 4X4 posts snapped.

South-southwest cross winds of 25 mph gusting to 38 mph at the Mammoth-Yosemite airport caused an experienced pilot to overcompensate and dip a wing of his Piper Mirage into the ground on takeoff. The wings and landing gear broke off. There were two people on board and the pilot suffered minor injuries.

Heavy snow fell mainly south and west of Susanville on the 10th and early on the 11th, with valleys below 5000 feet starting as rain or a mix of rain and snow before changing over to all snow. Six and a half to 8 inches of snow fell between Sierraville and Lake Davis, including Portola. Ten inches of snow was estimated from the Independence Creek SNOTEL.
A widespread 9 to 16 inches of snow fell around the Tahoe Basin on the 10th and 11th, including 12 to 13 inches in the Tahoe City area and 11 inches about 5 miles southwest of South Lake Tahoe.
Between 7 and 13 inches of snow fell in the Carson Range on the 10th and 11th, including 9 inches in Glenbrook, 7 to 10 inches in Incline Village and 13 inches at the Mount Rose Ski Area.
Wind gusts between 59 and 65 mph occurred at the Surprise Valley RAWS on the morning of the 13th.
Nine inches of snow fell in Loyalton, with 10 inches estimated from the Independence Creek SNOTEL (just east of Independence Lake).
Ten to 20 inches of snow fell near the Sierra crest, with 7 to 9 inches around Lake Tahoe, in Woodfords, and on the slopes of the Verdi Range (west of Verdi).
Fourteen to 20 inches of snow fell in the northern portion of the Carson Range, with 8 to 11 inches farther south in the Carson Range. At lake level, 5 inches of snow fell in Glenbrook.
Wind gusts between 58 and 67 mph were recorded on the north and northwest parts of Reno and in the Virginia Range on the morning of the 13th. Damage to a fence was reported in Reno-Stead.

Sustained winds of 40-50 mph with gusts 60-70 mph were noted at several locations, including the Fallon Naval Air Station, along Interstate 80 near Lovelock (Toulon NDOT), and along highway 50 in the Silver Springs and Stagecoach areas.

Two to 4 feet of snow fell above 7000 feet around the Lake Tahoe Basin on the 21st and 22nd. There was a mix of rain and snow below 6500 to 7000 feet, with minimal snowfall at lake level (1 to 3.5 inches Tahoe City and 1/2 inch in South Lake Tahoe) with mainly rain.
One to two feet of snow fell above 7000 feet, including 18 inches at Daggett Pass. Up to 8 inches of snow fell down to around 6700 feet, with mainly rain below that level around Lake Tahoe.

Wind gusts of 60 to 65 mph were recorded along I-580 and highway 395 in the north valleys of Reno and in the Washoe and Carson Valleys. Winds were sustained over 40 mph for a time as well. Wind prone areas along I-580 south of Reno reported wind gusts between 73 and 88 mph.

An estimated 8 to 10 inches of snow fell southwest of Susanville in the higher elevations per SNOTEL and HADS sensors. In the lower elevations, 5 inches of snow was noted at the Portola CO-OP station.
Five inches of snow fell in Cedarville between late evening on the 23rd and the morning of the 24th.

Eighteen to 24 inches of snow fell at ski areas and along and west of highway 89 on the 24th. Elsewhere, a widespread 10 to 14 inches of snow fell around Lake Tahoe, in Truckee, and east to the foothills of the Verdi Range.
Between 12 and 22 inches of snow fell in the northern portion of the Carson Range on the 24th, with 8 to 11 inches farther south around Lake Tahoe and in the southern portions of the Carson Range.

A ski instructor exited into the backcountry from the Sugar Bowl ski area on the afternoon of the 14th. When he failed to return home that night, he was reported missing (on the 15th). Tracking and location information from his phone placed him  on the backside of Mount Judah in an area with recent avalanche activity...however, inclement weather forced the suspension of the search on the 19th. ||On February 29, search and rescue teams using the cell phone information and dogs located the skier under 5 feet of snow. The time of the avalanche was estimated by the Sierra Avalanche Center.
Five to 8 inches of snow fell in the lower valleys from between a few miles southwest of Susanville to Portola. Only 2 inches of snow fell in Susanville.

The area in and near Virginia City reported between 9 and 12 inches of snow. Lesser amounts of 1 to 4 inches were noted in the Reno area down to 4800 to 5000 feet. Little or no snow (mainly rain) fell on the valley floors.

Sustained winds between 40-50 mph with gusts between 60 and 70 mph were recorded in the foothills north and northwest of Reno and in the Carson Valley, including along highway 395 and Interstate 580. In the wind-prone areas in and near Washoe Valley wind gusts reached as high as 90 mph. Damages from the high winds include: an uprooted 2-ft diameter tree in Carson City, 6 snapped power poles on Mount Rose highway, and fence damage near Cold Springs.

Downslope winds off the Pine Nut Range brought sustained winds of 35-50 mph with gusts up to 75 mph to the Smith Valley.  Highway 95 near Hawthorne experienced wind gusts up to 68 mph  (Walker Lake NDOT) during the evening of the 29th.
Five to 7 inches of snow fell from Portola to Susanville, respectively, on the 31st with most of the snow falling before 0900PST.

Between 20 and 31 inches of snow fell near the Sierra crest, with about 12 inches at the Mammoth Ranger Station. Much less snow fell near highway 395 with between 5 and 6.5 inches near Lee Vining and only 1.5 inches in Bridgeport.

Widespread snow totals of 4 to 8 inches were reported around the Reno-Sparks area, with lesser amounts between 2 and 5 inches farther south. Areas in and near the foothills west of Reno received between 8 and 10 inches of snowfall. Heavy, lake-effect snow off of Pyramid Lake caused whiteout conditions near Wadsworth, with two jackknifed big rigs causing the closure of westbound Interstate 80 in the evening.

Interstate 80 was closed (time range estimated) due to a 25-car pileup near the California and Nevada state line caused by snow and ice on the freeway. The accident was on the eastbound side of the freeway; however, the westbound side of I-80 had to be closed to allow emergency vehicles to reach the scene and get injured persons to the hospital.

A station 2.6 miles west-northwest of Fernley received a storm total of 11 inches of snow. This was enhanced substantially by lake-effect snow off of Pyramid Lake during the afternoon and evening of the 31st. In addition to snow, ASOS and AWOS observations from the Lovelock, Silver Springs and Fallon airfields indicated sustained winds in the 15 to 25 mph range, with gusts 30 to 40 mph in the afternoon and evening of the 31st. This caused blowing snow with visibilities generally between 1 and 3 miles, but occasionally below 1 mile.

A station located 3.4 miles south-southwest of Yerington reported a storm total snowfall of 9.5 inches. In addition to snow, widespread winds of 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 35 mph caused blowing and drifting snow, with visibilities in Hawthorne and Yerington often below 3 miles, and sometimes briefly down to between 1/2 and 3/4 of a mile.

Two avalanches hit Alpine Meadows Road the morning of the 18th, affecting a bus and two cars. The bus impacted a garage and caused damage, while the occupants of one car had to be dug out by fire and ski area officials. No injuries were noted due to the avalanches. Alpine Meadows Ski area was closed for the day due to high avalanche danger.

At least 3 large trees were downed the morning of the 18th in Mammoth Lakes. In at least one case, the heavy snow and gusty winds combined with a weakened tree (rotten inside) to cause the downing. One home was nearly split in two, with a nearby condominium unit rendered unlivable.

Between 6 and 11.5 inches of snow fell between Eagle Lake and Susanville south to near Portola and Blairsden. At the higher elevations, between 11 and 16 inches (estimated) fell at the Grizzly Ridge HADS and Independence Creek SNOTEL.

The Reno-Tahoe International airport recorded sustained winds over 40 mph for at least an hour during the afternoon of the 17th, with a gust to 58 mph at 1423PST. The NDOT sensor along Highway 395 in the Cold Springs Valley noted sustained winds as high as 47 mph. In the foothills south and southwest of Reno (including I-580) and in the Virginia Range, wind gusts 60-66 mph were recorded. The winds uprooted several trees and damaged a large sculpture in the Reno-Sparks area, and caused a transformer in Virginia City to blow out with a several-hour power outage.

A widespread 1 to 2 feet of snow was reported by the morning of the 18th. Snowfall rates were moderate to heavy with almost 13 inches in 8 hours in Tahoma and 24 inches at Tahoe-Donner in less than 12 hours.
Twelve to 18 inches of snow fell near the crest and along highway 395 north of Bridgeport (near Devil's Gate Summit), with lesser amounts of 5 to 10 inches elsewhere.
Twelve to 22 inches of snow were reported by cooperative observers through the morning of the 18th, highest at the Glenbrook Fire Station (22 inches).

Four to 8 inches of snow fell in west and southwest Reno as well as the Carson City-Minden area, with 3 to 6 inches in the Virginia Highlands. One to 3 inches of snow were reported in many areas near and east of 395, although Sparks generally received less than an inch.

Two rounds of snow brought between 2 and 4.5 feet of snow above 6500 feet, mainly west of highway 89. Below 6500 feet and farther east, considerably less snow fell with around a foot in the Tahoma and Tahoe City areas, with only 6 inches for the South Lake Tahoe and Truckee airports.

One to 3 feet of snow fell near the crest above 7500 feet from the evening of the 5th through the morning of the 6th. Elsewhere, snowfall totals dropped off substantially, with 9 inches at the Mammoth Ranger Station, 3 to 6 inches in Lee Vining, and 1.5 inches in Bridgeport.

Winds of 40 and 55 mph with gusts 60 to 80 mph were recorded in and just east of the foothills of the Carson Range south of Reno on the 13th. More isolated high winds were noted at the Reno-Stead airport (sustained 40 with gusts to 58) and the UNR Agricultural Farm (gust to 64 mph). The high winds caused a big rig to overturn on highway 395 near Stead. Finally, severe turbulence aloft near the Reno-Tahoe airport caused delays and cancellations on the morning of the 13th.

Southwest winds sustained between 40 and 54 mph with gusts 60 to 81 mph were recorded at the Mammoth-Yosemite airport and the Valentine Eastern Sierra Reserve (both near highway 395), with the higher end of the wind range at the latter location.

Between 18 and 30 inches of snow fell fell near the Sierra crest and in the higher elevations south of Lake Tahoe. At lake level, periods of rain or rain mixed with snow cut down totals greatly with only 9 inches of snow in Tahoma and just under 6 inches at the South Lake Tahoe airport and in Tahoe City.

Between 10 and 14 inches of snow fell on the shores of Lake Davis, with an estimated 14 to 24 inches near the Sierra crest and at around 7000 feet on Grizzly Ridge (northwest of Portola). Below 5000 feet, much less snowfall was reported with only 1 inch noted in Portola.

A widespread 4 to 8 inches of snow fell north of highway 50, with 9 to 12 inches for areas north and east of Reno including Sparks/Spanish Springs and Palomino Valley (just southwest of Pyramid Lake). Snowfall rates were heavy with most of the snow falling within 3 to 6 hours. The heavy, wet snow caused a tree to topple onto a car in Sparks.
Ten to 18 inches of snow fell near the Sierra crest above 6500-7000 feet and in the higher elevations south of Lake Tahoe, with 5 to 10 inches below 6500 feet and around the shores of Lake Tahoe.
Dime-size hail covered the ground in and near the Somersett community in northwest Reno.

A line of thunderstorms approximately 15 to 30 miles west of Fallon produced outflow winds as high as 49 mph gusting to 60 mph at the Naval Air Station in Fallon. Visibility was reduced to between 1 and 2 miles as the wind kicked up large amounts of dust.

Rough water due to gusty winds between 20 and 35 mph caused a paddleboarder to fall from his board into Lake Tahoe while seeking help for his companions who had also fallen from their boards. After the others were rescued by a marina crew, the rescue crew looked for the victim but he could not be found (although his board was found). The search for the victim was called off on June 15th.

A combination of heavy fuels and gusty winds caused the Tule Fire to run down the slopes of the Virginia Mountains in the Hardscrabble Canyon area on the 29th. The fire burned 10 structures (including 4 unoccupied homes) and 2 vehicles and forced the evacuation of about 600 persons in Sutcliffe. The fire also knocked out power in the town for several days. A declaration of disaster was made for the reservation and Pyramid Lake was closed for recreation until August 5th.
Major fire fighting efforts for the Virginia Fire Complex ended on the 4th. Pyramid Lake was re-opened for recreational use on the 5th by the Paiute Tribe.
Storm-total snowfall amounts:||near Westwood, 18 inches;|5 miles west of Beckwourth, 4.3 inches (at 4860 feet);|Susanville, 4 inches.

Storm-total snowfall amounts:||5 miles north of Alpine Meadows, 12 inches (at 6000 feet);|5 miles north of Truckee, 12 inches (at 6000 feet);|5 miles SW of Prosser Creek Reservoir near Tahoe Donner, 9 inches (at 7240 feet);|4 miles north of Meyers (between South Lake Tahoe and Fallen Leaf Lake), 9 inches (at 6340 feet);|2.5 miles north of Truckee, 8 inches (at 6250 feet);|6 miles WSW of Boca Reservoir, 8 inches;|.

Freezing fog, reducing visibilities to less than one-quarter mile at times, stretched across southern Pershing and northern Churchill Counties overnight.  The main areas affected were along Interstate 80 from just east of Fernley to the Rye Patch Reservoir, and along U. S. Highway 95 between Fallon and Trinity Junction.

Weather observations from the area around Hawthorne showed visibilities of less than one-quarter mile in fog. Satellite imagery also confirmed areas of fog east of Hawthorne and spreading north along U. S. Highway 95 to near Schurz.

A combination of steep terrain (cliff face) and significant rain caused a large rockfall onto Tioga Pass Road (CA 120), causing the shutdown of the road. The time of the rockfall is estimated and based around the time of the heavy rainfall.

Strong winds blowing from west to east across June Lake caused very choppy waters on the 15th. Five males (none wearing life jackets) were in a boat which capsized, causing the death of three of the males. Two of the men reached shore and were treated and released. The three victims were found by divers on the morning of the 18th.
High winds along Highway 395 between Susanville and Doyle caused the overturning of two semis between 0230PST and 0300PST. Power lines were downed due to fallen tree limbs in Susanville.
Wind gust recorded at the Surprise Valley RAWS.

Sustained winds of 35 to 45 mph with gusts up to 74 mph were recorded early on the 14th, mainly for the North Valleys of Reno, the foothills of the Carson Range, and in Washoe Valley. These winds were responsible for the rapid spread of the Little Valley wildfire and for a number of delays and cancellations at the Reno-Tahoe International airport.

A prescribed burn that was thought to be mopped up on October 13th flared up as high winds affected the Carson Range early on the 14th. The Little Valley Fire burned through 2,291 acres and destroyed 23 homes and 17 outbuildings. According to a Reno Gazette Journal investigation, the estimated value of 18 of the homes exceeded 26 million dollars with an independent fire consultant indicating that damages could exceed 80 million. The Little Valley RAWS measured a wind gust of 87 mph around 130 AM PDT on the 14th, close to the time of the wildfire start.

Sustained winds over 40 mph with gusts 58 to 64 mph were recorded on the 19th along the Highway 395/Interstate 580 corridor, including at the Reno-Tahoe International Airport, in the Carson Valley, and for the Reno-Stead area. In the foothills south and southwest of Reno winds gusted between 65 and 75 mph, with gusts as high as 81 mph at the Galena RAWS.
A National Weather Service cooperative observer reported 4 inches of snowfall in Cedarville.
The California Highway Patrol reported large boulders on Interstate 80 just west of the Donner Lake Interchange. A pickup truck ran into one of the boulders resulting in an injury.

A quote from the Sierra Avalanche Center: Two skiers hiked into closed uncontrolled terrain at Mt. Rose.  The first skier triggered a large avalanche that swept him 600-1000 ft downslope and buried him in debris that averaged 5 ft deep and reached up to 10 ft. deep in some areas. The second skier immediately called 911 and the search for his partner continued for the rest of the day. The skier was found deceased around midday on the 11th.
Wind gust measured at the Surprise Valley RAWS.
Gusts between 59 and 71 mph were recorded along Highway 395 between Lee Vining and the Mammoth Airport, as well as in the Chalfant Valley at the Benton RAWS.

Snowfall between 39 and 56 inches (3 to 5 feet) was reported at the Mammoth Ski area at and above 9000 feet. The June Mountain ski area noted 3 feet of snowfall at around 10,000 feet  (but only 10 inches at 7500 feet). Elsewhere along the crest, an estimated (from SNOTEL data) 14 to 27 inches of snow fell above 8500 feet. Below 8000 feet, up to 4 inches was reported as precipitation fell mainly as rain.
Wind gusts between 63 (Bulls Eye) and 89 (Galena) mph were recorded along Mount Rose Highway on the 15th.

Gusts between 73 and 89 mph were recorded in and near the Carson Range southwest of Reno and west of Carson City and Minden, with gusts between 60 and 70 mph along Highway 395 in the north valleys of Reno.  A semi truck was blown over in Washoe Valley at around 530PST. At the Reno-Tahoe International airport, at least 11 flights were cancelled, with at least 5 diversions, due to winds and turbulence.
Widespread wind gusts of 58 to 64 mph (64 mph at Walker Lake NDOT) were noted on the morning of the 15th, with sustained winds around 40 mph at times in the Smith Valley.

Mammoth Mountain Ski area reported between 20 and 32 inches of snowfall on the 23rd, with 14 inches in Mammoth Lakes at 8200 ft. Eight to 15 inches is estimated to have fallen for Sierra crest and Sweetwater Range SNOTEL sites. For locations along Highway 395 between Bridgeport and Crowley Lake, 2.5 to 5.5 inches of snow fell.

A weather spotter reported local blizzard conditions around the Mammoth Lakes area overnight. Visibilities were less than 100 feet at times with wind gusts to 70 mph. There was a total of 24 to 30 inches of snowfall overnight in Mammoth Lakes with up to 36 inches at the higher elevations including Mammoth Mountain Ski Resort.
A wind gust of 58 kt (67 mph) was recorded at the Truckee airport.
A 70 kt (81 mph) wind gust was recorded at the Lundy Lake RAWS at an elevation of 7055 feet.

Nearly steady rainfall from 5:30 AM through 4:48 PM contributed to the third largest daily precipitation total in the last 100 years in Reno.  A total of 1.91 inches of precipitation was recorded at the Reno-Tahoe International Airport for January 4th.

A 40-foot-long break in the Truckee Canal released floodwater into portions of Fernley, Nevada on the morning of January 5th.  Local newspapers reported that approximately 1500 people had to be evacuated from their homes.  Water 2 to 4 feet deep affected as many as 500 homes.  The Reno Gazette-Journal newspaper reported that more than $1.75 million in federal disaster housing assistance had been provided.  In addition to this, Fernley city officials estimated that the cost to repair roads would be over $720,000.

Storm total snowfall between 43 and 70 inches was reported in the higher elevations (generally above about 7000 feet) of the Carson Range, with between 9 and 14 inches at lake level, between the 2nd and the 5th.
An estimated 12 inches of snow fell at the Sheldon SNOTEL, with higher amounts possible farther west closer to the Surprise Valley in eastern California.

Rain changed to snow on the afternoon of the 4th, with widespread snowfall totals of 4 to 6 inches in the Reno-Sparks area by the morning of the 5th. Areas farther north in the Palomino Valley and along Red Rock Road north of Stead received up to 8 inches. Lesser amounts between 1 and 4 inches fell south of the Reno-Sparks area.
Between 3 and 6 inches of snow fell in the Fallon area from the evening of the 4th into the morning of the 5th. Higher amounts between 6 and 9 inches fell between Sutcliffe and Fernley.
Heavy snow was noted between the evening of the 1st and early on the 5th, including 15 inches in Susanville, 19 inches in Portola, and 21 inches several miles southwest of Susanville.

Hefty snowfall amounts between 3 and 7 feet fell near and west of Highway 89 between the 2nd and 5th, with the higher amounts (5 or more feet) above 7000 feet. Below 7000 feet east of about Highway 89, much lower amounts fell (longer periods of rain) with between 14 and 22 inches noted. Interstate 80 was closed between 1700PST on the 4th and 0100PST on the 5th due to the heavy snow.

Storm total snowfall amounts reached between 40 and 84 (7 feet) inches for the Mammoth Mountain Ski area from the afternoon of the 3rd into the early morning of the 5th, with the highest amounts above 9000 feet. East of the immediate Sierra crest down to around 7000 feet, up to 14 to 19 inches of snow was reported. Below 7000 feet, amounts fell off dramatically with significant rainfall. Only 6 inches of snow fell in Lee Vining, with around 2.5 inches in Bridgeport.
The Cedarville Cooperative Observer reported 30 inches of snowfall between early morning on the 2nd and the afternoon of the 4th.
